items.title: Imaging in Systemic Sclerosis (Scleroderma).
items.abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) or scleroderma is a multisystem autoimmune disorder characterized by a variable pattern of skin thickening and involvement of visceral organs. The pathophysiology is similar across all organs, which is chronic low-grade inflammation, with vasculopathy and eventual fibrosis. Diagnosis is primarily clinical, particularly in patients with established disease comprising characteristic skin and visceral manifestations, with a supportive role of laboratory and imaging findings. The presence of radiologic signs such as hidebound bowel or a combination of patulous lower esophageal sphincter, pulmonary fibrosis, skin thickening, and Raynaud phenomenon is relatively specific for SSc. Nevertheless, imaging in SSc is primarily used to determine the pattern, severity, and complications of visceral organ involvement, rather than for diagnosis of SSc. Radiologic evaluation in SSc employs a wide gamut of investigations, depending on the organ of interest. For example, US is used for the skin and superficial tissues; fluoroscopy, CT, or MR enterography for the gastrointestinal tract; endoanal US or MRI for the internal anal sphincter; high-resolution CT for the lungs; echocardiography and cardiac MRI for SSc-related pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) and cardiac disease; and radiography, CT, or MRI for musculoskeletal involvement. Early diagnosis of treatable features, such as PAH and gastroesophageal reflux, can help reduce the morbidity and mortality associated with SSc. Imaging is additionally useful to prognosticate and monitor the disease. The authors focus on the multisystem, multimodality imaging manifestations of SSc with relevant differential diagnoses to bridge the gaps in knowledge about SSc. © RSNA, 2026.

items.title: A rare presentation of probable catastrophic antiphospholipid syndrome with bilateral adrenal hemorrhage.
items.abstract: Catastrophic antiphospholipid syndrome (APS), a rare thrombotic manifestation of APS, is associated with high mortality. Rarely, it can present with bilateral adrenal hemorrhage (BAH). This case highlights a rare presentation of BAH due to probable catastrophic APS secondary to systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). A 57-year-old female with diabetes presented with hypovolemic shock, abdominal pain, and vomiting. Imaging revealed BAH; antiphospholipid antibodies were present in high titers in the blood. Antinuclear antibody and antidouble-stranded deoxyribonucleic acid antibody (anti-dsDNA) were positive in high titers. Catastrophic APS secondary to SLE was diagnosed. Serum morning cortisol was at 9.2 μg/dL (SI: 254 nmol/L) (reference range: 5-25 μg/dL [SI: 138-635 nmol/L]), and adrenocorticotropic hormone was at 180 pg/mL (SI: 39.6 pmol/L) (reference range: 10-60 pg/mL [SI: 1.6-13.9 pmol/L]); which indicated evolving primary adrenal insufficiency. The patient received pulse methylprednisolone, intravenous immunoglobulin, anticoagulants, and mycophenolate mofetil. Oral glucocorticoid was continued with regular monitoring of adrenal function. Mineralocorticoid replacement was not needed as the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system axis was intact. This report contributes to the sparse literature on catastrophic APS-related BAH, highlighting the need for early diagnosis and combined immunosuppressive and anticoagulant treatment.

items.title: Enhancing sexual health in women with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE): A mixed-methods systematic review of effective strategies.
items.abstract: IntroductionSexual dysfunction is highly prevalent among women with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and significantly impairs quality of life, intimate relationships, and psychological well-being. Despite its clinical relevance, sexual health is rarely addressed in routine rheumatology care, and evidence on effective interventions remains fragmented.ObjectivesThis mixed-methods systematic review aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of pharmacological and non-pharmacological interventions for improving sexual health outcomes in women with SLE while qualitatively synthesizing barriers and patient perspectives to inform multidisciplinary care.MethodsThis review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines (PROSPERO ID: CRD420250652901). PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and ScienceDirect were searched for original studies published between 2000 and 2025. Eligible studies included randomized controlled trials and qualitative research evaluating sexual health interventions in women with SLE. Methodological quality was assessed using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT, 2018). Due to heterogeneity in study populations, interventions, and outcome measures, findings were narratively synthesized.ResultsFive studies met the inclusion criteria, comprising four randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and one qualitative descriptive study. Non-pharmacological interventions-including Extended Permission, Limited Information, Specific Suggestions, and Intensive Therapy (EX-PLISSIT)-based sexual counseling, supportive-expressive psychotherapy and patient education-consistently improved sexual function and intimacy. Pharmacological interventions demonstrated mixed effects: low-dose dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA) was associated with improvements in sexual function and mental well-being, whereas transdermal testosterone patches showed no significant benefit. Inadequate communication and lack of routine sexual health assessment by rheumatologists were identified as major barriers to care.ConclusionSexual dysfunction in women with SLE is common yet underrecognized. Non-pharmacological interventions, particularly psychosexual counseling, appear effective and accessible, while pharmacological evidence remains inconclusive. Integrating sexual health into multidisciplinary rheumatology care through systematic screening, education, and interprofessional collaboration is essential.

items.title: Effect of Tocilizumab on Bone Outcomes in Patients with Rheumatoid Arthritis: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Tocilizumab (TCZ), an interleukin-6 receptor inhibitor for rheumatoid arthritis (RA), may benefit bone metabolism. This meta-analysis aimed to synthesize the effects of TCZ on bone turnover markers (BTMs) and bone mineral density (BMD). Cochrane Library, Embase, PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception to 23 February 2025. Randomized controlled trials and observational studies comparing TCZ with controls and reporting BTMs or BMD were included. Pooled mean differences (MDs) or standardized mean differences (SMDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated. Eight studies involving 1,221 participants were included. TCZ significantly reduced C-terminal telopeptide of type I collagen (CTX-I) (MD = -0.05, 95% CI [-0.08, -0.02], P = 0.001; I2 = 0%) and carboxyterminal telopeptide of type I collagen (ICTP) (MD = -7.19, 95% CI [-12.39, -1.99], P = 0.007; I2 = 97%), and increased procollagen type I N-terminal propeptide (PINP) (SMD = 0.21, 95% CI [0.08, 0.34], P = 0.001; I2 = 0%). The overall effect on osteocalcin (OC) was not significant, whereas RCT subgroup analysis showed a significant increase (MD = 3.83, 95% CI [1.12, 6.54], P = 0.006). No significant improvement in femoral neck BMD or lumbar spine BMD was observed. TCZ may improve bone metabolism in RA by suppressing bone resorption and promoting bone formation. However, these biochemical changes did not translate into measurable increases in BMD during follow-up. Further long-term studies are warranted to clarify effects on BMD.

items.title: Humanistic Burden of Sjögren's Disease: A Systematic Review of Treatment Efficacy on Health-Related Quality of Life.
items.abstract: Sjögren's disease (SjD) is a chronic autoantibody-driven inflammatory disorder that imposes a significant burden on afflicted patients. SjD is widely underappreciated, underdiagnosed, and undertreated. This may be partly due to the absence of advanced targeted treatments addressing the root cause of the disease. While some drugs are prescribed to help improve symptoms, many patients report inadequate relief, with disease progression and frequent organ damage. This systematic literature review (SLR) assessed the effects of treatments on patients' health-related quality of life (HRQoL). This study was supplemented by a patient focus group to gain additional insight into the humanistic burden of SjD. The SLR was conducted using MEDLINE and Embase (OvidSP) results between January 1, 2014, and February 2, 2026, supplemented with bibliographies, Google Scholar, disease-specific websites, and conference proceedings. Articles were screened specifically for HRQoL outcomes, including patient-reported disease-specific instruments (e.g., EULAR Sjögren's Syndrome Patient-Reported Index [ESSPRI]) and other tools focusing separately on fatigue and ocular/oral dryness. A small patient focus group (N = 4) provided further perspectives on disease burden and management. Fifty-three records were identified from 44 unique studies related to systemic treatments, including large case series and randomized controlled trials of traditional immunomodulatory or anti-inflammatory agents and newer biological treatments (e.g., rituximab, abatacept, hydroxychloroquine, leflunomide, corticosteroids, iguratimod, dazodalibep, telitacicept). Most systemic treatments provided no meaningful improvements in fatigue or ocular/oral dryness. SjD focus group participants reported persistent, overlapping symptoms, particularly fatigue and cognitive impairment, that limit daily activities. Participants expressed dissatisfaction with current treatments and a strong desire for holistic therapies that address the root cause, improve symptoms, and prevent disease progression. Systemic treatments have generally focused on disease activity parameters and have shown limited efficacy in reducing patient-reported symptoms as measured using HRQoL tools in SjD, leaving a significant unmet need for patient-centered holistic therapies.

items.title: How similar are siblings with familial Mediterranean fever? A pairwise analysis of clinical concordance.
items.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate intrafamilial concordance in clinical manifestations, disease severity, and treatment outcomes among affected sibling pairs carrying the same MEFV genotype, and thereby assess whether one sibling's disease course might help inform clinical expectations, monitoring, and individualized management of the other sibling. This retrospective cohort study included 222 patients from 111 affected sibling pairs carrying the same MEFV genotype who were followed at three tertiary pediatric rheumatology centers. Clinical manifestations, laboratory findings, disease severity scores, and treatment characteristics were recorded. Concordance for categorical variables was evaluated using Cohen's kappa (κ) coefficient, and intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC) were calculated for continuous variables. The median age at diagnosis was 77 months (range 8-214), with a median diagnostic delay of 13 months (range 0-160). The most common clinical manifestations were abdominal pain (79.7%), fever (64.9%), and arthralgia (59.0%). Homozygous M694V was the predominant genotype (45.0%). The median annual attack frequency decreased from 10 (range 0-30) before treatment to 1 (range 0-18) after colchicine therapy. Biologic therapy was required in 14.0% of patients. Concordance between siblings was generally low for most clinical features (κ = 0.095-0.393). Disease severity scores showed slight-to-moderate concordance (ICC = 0.181-0.410). Slight concordance was observed for attack frequency before (ICC = 0.193) and fair concordance after colchicine treatment (ICC = 0.225). Siblings with FMF demonstrated considerable phenotypic variability despite carrying the same MEFV genotype, indicating that the MEFV genotype alone does not fully explain intrafamilial disease expression. Other genetic, epigenetic, environmental, or individual-level factors may be involved; however, their contributions were not directly assessed in this study. • Familial Mediterranean fever shows marked phenotypic variability, even among patients carrying the same MEFV genotype. • Data on the concordance of clinical manifestations, disease severity, and treatment outcomes among affected siblings are limited. • In 111 sibling pairs carrying the same MEFV genotype, most clinical manifestations, attack frequencies, disease severity measures, and treatment outcomes showed low concordance. • Pleuritis showed substantial concordance; however, its low frequency and wide confidence interval preclude firm conclusions. Overall, the findings support individualized assessment even among siblings carrying the same MEFV genotype.

items.title: Perspectives of rheumatologists on the management of late-onset rheumatoid arthritis: a nationwide cross-sectional survey.
items.abstract: With population ageing, the number of patients with late-onset rheumatoid arthritis (LORA) is increasing. However, optimal treatment strategies remain unclear. We aimed this study to clarify the current perspectives of rheumatologists regarding the management of LORA. We conducted an anonymous online questionnaire for members of the Japan College of Rheumatology between March and May 2023. The questionnaire consisted of multiple-choice questions about their perspectives on the concept and management of LORA in clinical practice, and on treatment choices based on case vignettes. We aggregated and analysed the responses. A total of 1041 rheumatologists responded to the survey. The most common definition of LORA was '70 years' (n = 392, 38%), followed by '65 years' (n = 287, 28%) and '75 years' (n = 251, 24%). In the management of LORA, 60% (n = 624) of respondents answered that 'safety' is the top priority, followed by 'control of disease activity' (n = 277, 27%). However, most rheumatologists set a treatment goal of 'low disease activity' (n = 545, 52%) rather than 'remission' (n = 330, 32%). The most common response regarding issues when treating LORA was 'comorbidities/complications' (n = 693, 67%), followed by 'adverse events/safety' (n = 620, 60%) and 'cognitive function' (n = 448, 43%). The case vignette revealed that treatment choices for LORA patients are highly variable and affected by many factors, including comorbidities, cognitive function, living environment, activities of daily living, and financial status. This nationwide survey conducted in Japan revealed the challenges rheumatologists face and the diversity of their preferences and perceptions regarding the management of LORA in clinical practice.

items.title: Frequency of difficult-to-treat rheumatoid arthritis and associated factors at b/tsDMARD initiation in a tertiary referral center: a cross-sectional study.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic inflammatory rheumatic disease in which adequate disease control remains challenging in a subset of patients despite the availability of numerous therapeutic agents. In 2021, the European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology (EULAR) established the definition of difficult-to-treat rheumatoid arthritis (D2T-RA). To determine the frequency of D2T-RA among RA patients treated with biological or targeted synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (b/tsDMARDs) and to examine factors recorded at b/tsDMARD initiation that were associated with subsequent D2T-RA classification. In this single-center cross-sectional study, D2T-RA status was assessed at an index visit conducted between April and November 2023. D2T-RA status was determined at the index visit using a study-specific operationalization of the European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology (EULAR) definition. Treatment-initiation data were collected retrospectively. Clinically selected multivariable models were adjusted for the interval from b/tsDMARD initiation to the index visit. Analyses were repeated after removing the Health Assessment Questionnaire (HAQ) item from the definition. Of the 487 patients included, 181 (37.1%) met the operationalized D2T-RA criteria. None of the factors in the primary model was independently associated with D2T-RA classification. In the model without the 28-joint Disease Activity Score based on erythrocyte sedimentation rate (DAS28-ESR), higher HAQ was associated with D2T-RA (OR 1.56, 95% CI 1.03-2.36; p = 0.036). Removing the HAQ-based item reclassified 23 patients and reduced the frequency to 32.4%. With this outcome, younger age at diagnosis (OR 0.972, 95% CI 0.949-0.996; p = 0.023) and higher body mass index (OR 1.055, 95% CI 1.008-1.103; p = 0.020) were associated with D2T-RA in the primary model. D2T-RA was common in this tertiary cohort of patients receiving b/tsDMARDs. The primary model did not identify an independently associated baseline factor, whereas higher HAQ, younger age at diagnosis, and higher BMI were associated with D2T-RA in additional models. As these associations were not consistent across models, they should be interpreted cautiously..

items.title: Screening for Neoehrlichia mikurensis and other emerging tick-borne pathogens in Swedish patients with systemic lupus erythematosus receiving B-cell-targeted therapies.
items.abstract: The management of moderate to severe systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) has advanced considerably with the introduction of B-cell-targeted therapies. Several emerging tick-borne diseases (eTBDs) have gained increasing attention as causes of febrile illness with potentially serious complications in predominantly immunocompromised, B-cell-depleted individuals. Since the occurrence of eTBDs remains insufficiently studied in SLE, we aimed to determine whether such infections remain undetected among patients living in a tick-endemic region of Southeastern Sweden. Biobanked sera (n = 143) collected during 2015-2024 from 48 SLE patients receiving rituximab or belimumab in Region Östergötland were included. As comparators, samples from patients with quiescent disease on hydroxychloroquine treatment only (n = 50) were analysed. All samples were investigated by real-time polymerase chain reaction assays for the presence of the eTBD pathogens Neoehrlichia mikurensis, Borrelia burgdorferi sensu lato, Borrelia miyamotoi, Anaplasma phagocytophilum, Spiroplasma ixodetis , and Babesia spp. No pathogen-specific DNA for the examined eTBDs was detected in serum samples from the included patients. Evidence suggests that B-cell-targeted therapies may raise eTBD risk; however, none of the individuals with SLE included herein was found to be infected, despite the documented presence of these pathogens in Southeastern Sweden. Our findings contrast with those from Norwegian immunocompromised patients, but are in line with data from the Danish nationwide Rheumatological Database, including patients with arthritis receiving tumour necrosis factor inhibitors. Hypothetically, higher doses of glucocorticoids impair B-cell function and increase the risk of eTBD further. Nevertheless, routine eTBD screening of patients with SLE in Southeastern Sweden is not supported by our data.

items.title: Clinical Characteristics and Mortality Outcomes in Cancer-Associated Dermatomyositis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
items.abstract: Approximately 15% to 25% of adult dermatomyositis cases are associated with underlying cancers. To date, no study has comprehensively synthesized the available evidence on mortality in cancer-associated dermatomyositis. To explore the clinical characteristics, mortality, and survival outcomes of cancer-related dermatomyositis. MEDLINE, Embase, and PubMed were searched from inception to August 5, 2025 (PROSPERO CRD420251269785). Observational studies including at least 10 cases and reporting mortality outcomes among adults with cancer-associated dermatomyositis were eligible. Risk of bias and certainty of evidence were assessed using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation. Random-effects meta-analysis was used to estimate pooled survival outcomes. Twenty-three studies including 974 patients were analyzed with a mean age of 58 years and a female predominance. Head and neck cancers were the most frequently reported malignancies, reflecting population patterns. Muscle weakness, heliotrope rash, and dysphagia were common. Across 16 studies including 605 patients, cancer was diagnosed in the majority of cases (82%) within 2 years of dermatomyositis onset. Patients with cancer-associated dermatomyositis had higher mortality rates than those without malignancy, with worse 1- and 5-year survival (low certainty of evidence). Only 2 studies assessed mean survival time, with a pooled estimate of 4.57 years from dermatomyositis diagnosis (95% CI, 2.08-7.05; I 2  = 0%). This review synthesizes the available evidence on cancer-associated dermatomyositis and reinforces its association with poor prognosis. Larger studies with standardized reporting of serological profiles and mortality outcomes are needed to better characterize survival and prognostic factors.

items.title: Endothelial IFI16 drives vasculopathy and profibrotic remodeling in systemic sclerosis by activating JAK/STAT signaling.
items.abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is characterized by a prominent type I interferon (IFN-I) signature, yet the upstream drivers that link this signature to fibrosis remain unclear. This study aims to identify Interferon gamma-inducible protein 16 (IFI16) as an endothelial mediator that contributes to vasculopathy and fibrotic remodeling in SSc. Machine-learning screening of public bulk RNA-seq was applied to identify fibrosis-associated IFN-I regulators. IFI16 expression pattern was validated by scRNA-seq, spatial transcriptomics and immunofluorescence. Functional and pathway analyses were performed in IFI16-overexpressing endothelial cells. A machine-learning-based analysis of bulk RNA-seq datasets demonstrated that IFI16 is significantly upregulated in SSc skin and ranks among the IFN-I-associated genes positively correlated with more severe skin fibrosis, shorter non-Raynaud disease duration, and elevated extracellular matrix deposition. Single-cell and spatial transcriptomic analyses revealed the enrichment of IFI16 in endothelial cells, and the co-localization of IFI16 with vasculature was validated by immunofluorescence. IFI16-high endothelial cells exhibited higher IFN activity and enhanced extracellular matrix remodeling. Stimulation with profibrotic or proinflammatory cytokines (IL-6, IL-1β, TGF-β and IFN-⍺) upregulated IFI16 expression in endothelial cells. Gain-of-function experiments showed that IFI16 overexpression impaired endothelial proliferation, migration, and tube formation, while driving the transition of endothelial cells towards mesenchymal cells through JAK-STAT signaling. Inhibition of JAK-STAT signaling reversed IFI16-induced endothelial-mesenchymal transition. Collectively, endothelial IFI16 coupled IFN-I signaling to vasculopathy and fibrotic remodeling via JAK-STAT activation, highlighting IFI16 as a promising therapeutic target in SSc vasculopathy and the subsequent fibrosis.

items.title: Scleredema Diabeticorum Mimicking Systemic Sclerosis in a 75-Year-Old Female: A Case Report.
items.abstract: Scleredema diabeticorum is a rare sclerosing cutaneous disorder characterized by diffuse, nonpitting, woody skin induration, most commonly occurring in patients with long-standing diabetes mellitus. Its clinical resemblance to systemic sclerosis (SSc) may result in diagnostic confusion, particularly in atypical presentations. We report a 75-year-old woman with a 20-year history of insulin-dependent Type 2 diabetes mellitus who developed progressive, generalized skin thickening. The disease initially involved the lower extremities and subsequently progressed proximally to the trunk, upper limbs, and face, with prominent facial and periorbital involvement and sparing of the hands and feet. She was initially suspected to have SSc because of diffuse skin induration and positive antinuclear antibodies and was treated with corticosteroids. However, the absence of characteristic distal scleroderma features, negative SSc-specific antibody testing, and histopathological findings of marked dermal thickening with broad collagen bundles and mucin deposition supported a diagnosis of scleredema diabeticorum. Management was complicated by diabetic nephropathy and concurrent cardiac disease, requiring individualized immunomodulatory therapy, close monitoring, and optimization of glycemic control. UVA1 phototherapy was attempted but discontinued because of immediate clinical intolerance. The patient subsequently received systemic immunomodulatory treatment with clinical improvement during follow-up. This case highlights the importance of distinguishing scleredema diabeticorum from SSc, particularly when atypical clinical features and positive nonspecific autoantibodies may lead to diagnostic uncertainty. Careful clinical assessment, appropriate serological evaluation, and histopathology are essential for accurate diagnosis and management.

items.title: Oral glucocorticoids added to ILD-modifying therapy in systemic sclerosis-associated interstitial lung disease: a target trial emulation study from the EUSTAR database.
items.abstract: We aimed to estimate whether adding oral glucocorticoids to ILD-modifying therapy improves 12-month lung outcomes in systemic sclerosis-associated interstitial lung disease (SSc-ILD). We emulated a target trial using the EUSTAR database. Eligible adults with confirmed SSc-ILD initiated an eligible ILD-modifying therapy at baseline (T0), either alone or with oral glucocorticoids added (prednisone-equivalent dose ≤20 mg/day). Follow-up ended at the visit closest to 12 months within a 9 to 15-month window. The primary outcome was the between-group difference in change in FVC (% predicted). Secondary outcomes were progressive lung fibrosis and isolated DLCO decline ≥15%. We used multiple imputation (m=80), stabilised inverse probability of treatment weighting, robust variance estimators and Rubin's rules. Of 443 patients, 185 (41.8%) received oral glucocorticoids with ILD-modifying therapy and 258 (58.2%) received ILD-modifying therapy alone. Adding oral glucocorticoids was not associated with improved 12-month FVC. The adjusted mean difference in FVC change was -2.10 percentage points (95% CI -4.68 to 0.47; p=0.11). There was no clear difference in progressive lung fibrosis (RR 1.40, 95% CI 0.83 to 2.35) or isolated DLCO decline ≥15% (RR 0.81, 95% CI 0.39 to 1.69). Findings were consistent in the truncated-weight sensitivity analysis. Adding oral glucocorticoids to ILD-modifying therapy was not associated with improved 12-month FVC in SSc-ILD. items.title: Social and Structural Forces Shaping Reproductive Decision-Making in Hispanic Women with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus: A Qualitative Study.
items.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) disproportionately affects women of reproductive age, making pregnancy timing and contraception use central to care. Although clinical counseling is vital to reproductive planning, less is known about the sociocultural and structural influences shaping reproductive decision-making among Hispanic women with SLE in the United States. This study explored patient perspectives on multi-level factors influencing reproductive health decision-making. We conducted semi-structured interviews with 30 Hispanic women with SLE recruited from a safety-net rheumatology clinic and a community lupus support organization. Participants were aged 18-45 years, sexually active or considering pregnancy within three years, and fluent in English or Spanish. Interviews were conducted virtually, transcribed, and analyzed using a grounded theory-informed approach, with the Socioecological Model retrospectively applied to guide analysis. Four major themes aligned with the Socioecological Framework. Reproductive decision-making was shaped by structural stability, including financial security, career readiness, and confidence managing SLE during pregnancy. Culture and religion were present but variably integrated into reproductive health considerations, while partners and family members influenced how risks and decisions were discussed and supported. Participants also relied on informal information networks, including peer experiences and online resources, to interpret reproductive risks and contraception options. Reproductive planning among Hispanic women with SLE is influenced by structural, relational, and informational factors extending beyond the clinical encounter. These findings highlight the need for supportive interventions or resources beyond the clinical encounter, including supportive networks, trusted information, and peer-informed support tailored to young women living with SLE.

items.title: Multidimensional Patient-Reported Impact Profiles Based on the Seven RAID Domains in Patients with Rheumatoid Arthritis and Associated Factors: A Multicentre Latent Profile Analysis.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) affects patients across interconnected symptom, functional and psychosocial domains. The Rheumatoid Arthritis Impact of Disease (RAID) scale captures patient-reported impact across seven domains, but the distribution of overall impact levels and factors associated with profile membership remain insufficiently characterized. To identify latent profiles reflecting levels of patient-reported impact based on the seven RAID domains and examine factors associated with profile membership among patients with RA. A convenience sample of 338 patients with RA was recruited from 18 tertiary Grade A hospitals across 11 cities in China. The seven RAID domains were used as continuous indicators in latent profile analysis. The three-profile solution was retained based on classification quality, profile size, parsimony, and clinical interpretability, despite lower information criteria for the four-profile model. Differences in participant characteristics and factors associated with profile membership were examined using univariable analyses and multivariable multinomial logistic regression. Three ordered profiles were identified: low impact (n = 188, 55.6%), moderate impact (n = 113, 33.4%), and high impact (n = 37, 10.9%). Scores increased consistently across all seven RAID domains from the low- to high-impact profiles. Comorbidities and glucocorticoid use were associated with higher odds of membership in the moderate-impact profile, whereas conventional synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic drug use was associated with lower odds. Older age, lack of basic medical insurance and rural residence were associated with higher odds of membership in the high-impact profile, whereas greater self-management ability was associated with lower odds. Patients with RA could be differentiated into three ordered levels of patient-reported impact based on the seven RAID domains. Clinical, social and self-management characteristics were associated with membership in the moderate- or high-impact profiles.

items.title: Rituximab for the Treatment of ANCA-Associated Vasculitis: A Real-World Cohort Study.
items.abstract: Antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)-associated vasculitis comprises multisystemic diseases treated with glucocorticoids combined with cyclophosphamide or rituximab. In Uruguay, the National Resources Fund (Fondo Nacional de Recursos, FNR) covers rituximab for selected patients with ANCA-associated vasculitis. This study aimed to describe the characteristics and clinical course of patients treated with rituximab under this coverage mechanism. An observational, analytical, retrospective cohort study was performed. Adult patients with ANCA-associated vasculitis whose rituximab treatment was approved by the FNR were included. Demographic, clinical, serologic, therapeutic, and safety variables were recorded. Baseline assessment, at the first rituximab cycle (T0), was compared with assessment at the second cycle (T1). Fifty-eight patients were included; 28 (48.3%) were women. Mean age was 58.6 (12.9) years. Granulomatosis with polyangiitis was the predominant clinical form (70.7%). Rituximab was used for refractory disease in 32 patients (55.2%) and for relapse in 26 (44.8%). Forty-three patients (74.1%) had a T1 assessment, with a median interval of 6.9 months between cycles. Median Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score (BVAS) fell from 18.5 points at T0 to 7.0 points at T1 (p < 0.001); 25 patients (58.1%) had a reduction of at least 50% from baseline. Median urine protein-to-creatinine ratio decreased from 0.395 to 0.05 g/g (p = 0.012). Median serum creatinine decreased from 1.3 mg/dL to 1.1 mg/dL (p = 0.11). Median daily prednisone dose fell from 30 to 5 mg/day (p < 0.001). Eight deaths were recorded (13.8%); four occurred within the first six months after the first rituximab dose. In this national cohort of patients with refractory or relapsing ANCA-associated vasculitis, rituximab was associated with a significant reduction in disease activity and glucocorticoid dose. Proteinuria also decreased significantly; serum creatinine did not. These findings provide real-world data on rituximab use in Uruguay and are consistent with international evidence.

items.title: Primary scrotal-wall leiomyosarcoma following unplanned excision: Positive deep margin and testis-sparing R0 re-excision in a patient with Behçet disease.
items.abstract: Primary scrotal-wall leiomyosarcoma is an exceptionally rare soft-tissue malignancy. We report a 65-year-old man with longstanding Behçet disease who presented with an 18-month progressively enlarging right scrotal-wall mass. Testis-sparing excision revealed a 4 × 3 × 2.8 cm low-grade tumor with focally positive surgical margins. Morphologic and immunohistochemical findings were consistent with leiomyosarcoma. Staging imaging showed no distant metastatic disease. Repeat wide local excision achieved an R0 resection while preserving the testis, with no recurrence or metastasis on subsequent imaging. This case highlights the consequences of unplanned sarcoma excision and the importance of margin-directed re-excision to achieve complete tumor clearance following R1 resection.

items.title: Pulmonary hypertension secondary to IgG4-related disease: a case report and literature review.
items.abstract: IgG4-related disease (IgG4-RD) is a fibroinflammatory condition that can involve multiple organs, including the kidneys, but pulmonary vascular involvement is rare. We present a 29-year-old Nepalese male with known IgG4-RD kidney involvement who developed progressive exertional dyspnea after two years of clinical stability on azathioprine. Chest imaging showed no underlying interstitial lung disease. Evaluation revealed severe pre-capillary pulmonary hypertension (PH) on right heart catheterization, with negative workup for common PH etiologies. After limited response to corticosteroid and azathioprine intensification, rituximab induction, followed by six-monthly maintenance cycles, was given while sildenafil and macitentan were continued. This led to marked clinical, biochemical, and hemodynamic improvement: NT-proBNP decreased from 1333 to 24 pg/mL, RVSP improved from 68 to 42.61 mmHg, and IgG4 decreased from 10.732 to 1.186 g/L. This case highlights that IgG4-RD can cause severe pre-capillary PH and may respond substantially to rituximab.

items.title: Stroke in postpartum: a case report on rare presentation of primary Sjögren's syndrome.
items.abstract: Sjögren's syndrome is a systemic disease that can affect all organs. Postpartum stroke is a rare presentation of Sjögren's syndrome, requiring a multidisciplinary approach. A 10-day postpartum 28-year-old woman presented with an acute onset of right-sided weakness with deviation of the mouth to the left. She also complained of dryness of the eyes, generalized fatigability, and intermittent generalized aches and pains. On examination, power in the right upper and lower limbs was 1/5, with a right upper motor neuron-type facial palsy and a positive Babinski sign. Non-contrast computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging were diagnostic of an infarct involving the left frontal and parietal lobes. Carotid Doppler ultrasonography showed near-complete occlusion of the internal carotid artery. Tear film break-up time showed moderate dry eyes. Tests for rheumatological conditions showed a positive antinuclear antibody, and tests for extractable nuclear antigens showed positive anti-SS-A and anti-Ro-52. We diagnosed the case as a stroke due to clinically suspected Sjögren's syndrome-associated large-vessel vasculitis and started the patient on prednisolone, azathioprine, and hydroxychloroquine, with a steroid taper over 4 weeks. Postpartum stroke presents challenges in management because studies of thrombolytic therapy for stroke list pregnancy as an exclusion criterion. Our patient did not receive thrombolytic therapy; instead, she was managed with prednisolone, azathioprine, and hydroxychloroquine, with tapering of the steroid over 4 weeks. This case report highlights the challenges of postpartum stroke management and the roles of thorough investigations and interdisciplinary coordination.

items.title: Neglected chronic tophaceous gout complicated by massive ulceration and destructive polyarticular arthropathy: a case report.
items.abstract: Ulcerated tophaceous gout is a rare complication of chronic gout that may lead to severe joint destruction and disability. A 50-year-old farmer with longstanding untreated gout presented with a large non-healing ulcer over the right forefoot, multiple tophi, and destructive polyarticular arthropathy. Serum urate was only mildly elevated, while radiographs showed characteristic punched-out erosions with overhanging edges. The patient underwent surgical debridement followed by febuxostat, colchicine prophylaxis, wound care, and lifestyle modification. At 3 months, the ulcer had healed, serum urate had reached the treatment target (5.7 mg/dL), and pain and mobility had improved. This case illustrates the severe consequences of prolonged non-adherence to urate-lowering therapy (ULT), leading to neglected, advanced, ulcerated tophaceous gout with extensive joint destruction. Combined surgical debridement, optimized ULT, and meticulous wound care resulted in successful healing and functional improvement. Advanced ulcerated tophaceous gout may occur in neglected chronic gout. Early recognition and a combined surgical and medical approach can achieve favorable outcomes while preventing further disability.

items.title: Development of a Kyphosis Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation Technique in Patients with Spinal Mobility Restriction Due to Ankylosing Spondylitis.
items.abstract: Patients with ankylosing spondylitis (AS) often present with spinal rigidity and kyphotic deformity, which may hinder conventional cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR). This study describes a modified Kyphosis‑CPR (K‑CPR) technique developed to improve resuscitation in this population. A retrospective observational analysis was performed on 28 AS patients presenting with cardiac arrest between January 2010 and January 2025. During K‑CPR, two practitioners elevated the patient by the lower legs until the occiput touched the ground, achieving a near‑supine posture. The median age was 64.5 years, and 60.7% were male. Cardiovascular disease was the most common cause of arrest (46.4%), while asystole was the predominant rhythm (71.4%). Return of spontaneous circulation at 24 hours was achieved in 17.9% of patients. The outcomes were comparable to conventional CPR outcomes reported in the literature. Although limited by small sample size, K‑CPR appears feasible and may provide a practical alternative for AS patients with spinal immobility. Key Words: Ankylosing spondylitis, Cardiopulmonary resuscitation, Kyphosis, Emergency medicine, Return of spontaneous circulation.

items.title: Defective macrophage plasticity exacerbates progression of inflammation in patients with rheumatoid arthritis.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) affects over 1% of the global population. Current therapies cannot cure the disease, and only 20% of patients achieve long-term, drug-free remission. Recent studies highlight a dual role for synovial macrophages, which comprise both proinflammatory and remission-associated subsets. However, how macrophage plasticity and metabolic programming drive RA pathogenesis remains poorly understood. This study investigated how phenotypic and functional shifts in macrophage subsets contribute to chronic joint inflammation and bone erosion. Peripheral blood CD14+ monocytes from RA patients and healthy controls (HC) were differentiated into M1, M2a, M2b, M2c, and M2d macrophage subsets. To simulate the inflamed joint, cells were cultured under both atmospheric oxygen and hypoxic conditions. Phenotypic and chemokine receptor profiles were evaluated using RT-qPCR and multiparametric flow cytometry for a panel of markers, including CD14, CD11c, CD38, CD86, CD163, CD206, CD209, MerTK, IRF4, CCR1, CCR2, CCR4, CCR5, and CCR8. Metabolic characterization was performed via flow cytometric assessment of protein synthesis. To validate these phenotypes in vivo , scRNA-seq analysis (GSE200815) was conducted on synovial tissue macrophages from RA and HC individuals. Finally, the functional capacity of each macrophage subtype to differentiate into bone-resorbing osteoclasts was assessed. scRNA-seq data identified M1, M2a, M2b, M2c, and M2d clusters at comparable frequencies between HC and RA synovial tissues. However, RA macrophage subsets exhibited a distinct proinflammatory shift, characterized by increased CD86 and VEGF expression, and reduced MerTK expression. In vitro , RA-derived macrophages displayed altered metabolic activity and a similar pathogenic phenotype, which was particularly pronounced in the M2c subset compared to HCs. Hypoxia significantly exacerbated these phenotypic discrepancies in RA M2c macrophages. Functional assays revealed that all macrophage subsets, except M2c, successfully differentiated into osteoclasts, with RA-derived cells yielding significantly higher numbers of pathogenic osteoclasts. Dysregulated phenotypic, metabolic, and functional plasticity causes RA macrophages to adopt intermediate, pathogenic phenotypes. These alterations may impair tissue resolution, enhance osteoclastogenesis, and sustain chronic inflammation in the arthritic joint.

items.title: Case report: Progressive organ-threatening IgG4-related disease despite conventional immunosuppression: lessons from a 5-year longitudinal follow-up.
items.abstract: To describe the 5-year clinical course of a patient who progressed from IgG4-related dacryoadenitis and sialadenitis (IgG4-DS) to IgG4-related hypophysitis (IgG4-RH) and retroperitoneal fibrosis, evaluating the clinical course and treatment response to conventional immunosuppressive therapy through longitudinal clinical, serological, endocrine, and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) assessments. Clinical records were retrospectively reviewed, focusing on disease progression after treatment discontinuation, responses to sequential conventional synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (csDMARDs), and long-term pituitary endocrine outcomes. During 5 years of follow-up, a 44-year-old man with IgG4-DS developed partial anterior hypopituitarism, central diabetes insipidus, and retroperitoneal fibrosis following two episodes of unplanned treatment discontinuation. Serial MRI demonstrated progressive pituitary stalk thickening accompanied by heterogeneous enhancement. The maximum stalk diameter was 4.0 mm at diagnosis (May 2023), decreased to 3.6 mm during maintenance therapy (September 2024), increased to 8.5 mm at relapse (March 2025), and decreased to 7.0 mm after treatment modification (November 2025). Glucocorticoids combined with sequential csDMARDs controlled acute inflammation but failed to prevent permanent gonadal and posterior pituitary dysfunction. Serum IgG4 reached a peak of 38,100 mg/L, and its re-elevation preceded both clinical and radiological relapse. At the last assessment in January 2026, serum IgG4 remained elevated at 4,594 mg/L, with persistent hypogonadism and central diabetes insipidus. Disease progression occurred mainly during treatment interruption, while residual activity persisted despite conventional csDMARDs. The relative contributions of treatment non-adherence and limited treatment efficacy remain uncertain. Combined serum IgG4 and MRI monitoring may aid early detection of relapse, but this requires validation in larger cohorts.

items.title: Case Report: A rare case of biopsy-proven lupus nephritis complicated by Graves' disease in a 39-year-old man.
items.abstract: Hyperthyroidism and systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) are both common diseases in internal medicine. Among them, Graves' disease (GD) is the most frequent cause of hyperthyroidism, while lupus nephritis (LN) represents one of the most severe organ manifestations of SLE. Basic research suggests that GD and SLE may share overlapping genetic and immunological pathways; however, whether these shared mechanisms contribute to their clinical coexistence remains uncertain. Clinical studies or case reports on their coexistence are currently limited, and we cannot effectively manage cases of co-occurrence based on authoritative guidelines or expert consensus. In this study, we report a 39-year-old male patient with biopsy-proven ISN/RPS Class IV + V LN concomitant with GD. The patient was treated with a combination of glucocorticoids, mycophenolate mofetil, and hydroxychloroquine for LN, along with methimazole for GD, supplemented by symptomatic therapy including antihypertensive and heart rate controlling agents, etc. The patient demonstrated early clinical and laboratory improvement during follow-up, although the limited follow-up precluded assessment of an established renal response.

items.title: Therapeutic enhancement and toxicity reduction of total glucosides of paeony combined with conventional therapy in juvenile idiopathic arthritis: a meta-analysis and network pharmacology.
items.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of total glucosides of paeony (TGP) combined with conventional therapy in juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) and explore the network regulatory mechanisms underlying TGP's synergistic enhancement and toxicity reduction effects. We searched for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) on the efficacy of TGP combined with conventional therapy in JIA until 1 February 2026 (databases: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, SinoMed, Chinese National Knowledge Infrastructure, Wanfang, and VIP). The outcome measures included overall effective rate, adverse reactions, inflammation indicators, autoantibody levels, and clinical symptoms. Subsequently, an integrative pharmacology approach was employed to construct a "drug target-efficacy/toxicity gene" interaction network, elucidating potential molecular mechanisms of TGP's synergistic and toxicity-reducing effects. A total of 17 RCTs were included, involving 966 children with JIA. Compared with conventional Western medicine alone, TGP combination therapy significantly improved the overall response rate [risk ratio (RR) = 1.13, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.07-1.19, P  < 0.0001]and reduced the incidence of adverse events (RR = 0.63, 95% CI 0.43-0.91, P  = 0.02), markedly ameliorating serum inflammatory indicators [interleukin (IL)-1, IL-17, tumor necrosis factor α , C-reactive protein, and erythrocyte sedimentation rate], autoantibody levels, and clinical symptoms in JIA patients. The "drug target-efficacy/toxicity gene" interaction network revealed that TGP exerts synergistic effects primarily by regulating energy metabolism, alleviating oxidative stress and inflammation, and suppressing synovitis and osteoclastogenesis. Its toxicity-reducing effects were mediated through the inhibition of hepatic inflammation, oxidative stress, and angiogenesis, as well as modulation of lipid and amino acid metabolism. Notably, oxidative stress and lipid metabolism emerged as potential common mechanisms for TGP enhancement and toxicity reduction. The therapy of TGP combined with conventional Western medicine could enhance clinical efficacy and reduce adverse events in JIA patients. The synergistic and toxicity-reducing mechanisms of TGP might be associated with multi-pathway regulation, particularly involving oxidative stress and lipid metabolism.

items.title: Case Report: Prosthetic valve migration unmasking behçet disease after transcatheter aortic valve replacement.
items.abstract: Behçet disease (BD) is a systemic vasculitis with protean manifestations; concurrent skeletal and cardiovascular involvement is exceptionally rare and poses formidable diagnostic challenges. We report a 51-year-old woman who presented with multifocal osteolytic bone lesions and acneiform eruptions, initially fulfilling the Benhamou criteria for SAPHO syndrome. Severe aortic regurgitation was discovered, and transapical transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) was performed using the J-valve system to avoid sternotomy in the context of suspected active osteitis. At 3 months post-TAVR, the patient developed cerebral infarction and superior mesenteric artery thrombosis despite therapeutic anticoagulation. At 5 months, the prosthesis catastrophically dislodged into the left ventricular outflow tract. This event, occurring without evidence of infective endocarditis or procedural failure, prompted diagnostic reconsideration. The constellation of recurrent oral ulcers, acneiform lesions, multifocal osteolytic lesions, arterial thrombosis, and prosthetic valve dehiscence led to a revised diagnosis of BD-associated aortitis. Histopathological examination of the explanted tissue revealed lymphocytic infiltration and focal necrosis without infection. Following a 3-month course of immunosuppression, the patient underwent a Bentall procedure and remained asymptomatic with sustained cardiac reverse remodeling at 2-year follow-up. Prosthetic valve dehiscence in the absence of infection should be regarded as a sentinel diagnostic event for inflammatory aortitis, even when formal BD classification criteria are initially unmet. This case underscores the imperative of establishing a unifying diagnosis before committing to structural cardiac intervention in patients with concurrent systemic inflammatory features.

items.title: Comparing survival and clinical features of anti-MDA5 and anti-synthetase idiopathic inflammatory myopathy in a North American cohort.
items.abstract: Anti-synthetase syndrome (ASyS) and anti-MDA5 dermatomyositis (DM) cause significant morbidity and mortality due to interstitial lung disease (ILD). While large cohorts of these groups have been studied in Asia and Europe, data on clinical features and mortality risk within North America is limited. We aim to compare the mortality and clinical features between patients with anti-MDA5 DM and those with ASyS in a North American myositis cohort to identify predictors of mortality. A retrospective chart review was conducted in a large healthcare system. Patients were identified through specialty clinics, diagnosed with anti-MDA5 DM or ASyS by an expert clinician, and confirmed positive for anti-MDA5 or an ASyS antibody. Demographics, clinical features including baseline pulmonary function tests (PFTs) and high-resolution CT (HRCT), and treatment regimens were collected. Statistical analyses included t-test, Wilcoxon tests, Kaplan-Meier curves, and univariate Cox proportional hazards models. One hundred patients (50% with anti-MDA5 DM, 50% ASyS) were analyzed. Over a median follow-up of 7.4 years, 18 patients died (8 in the anti-MDA5 group, 10 in the ASyS group). The 10-year survival rates of the two groups were similar. items.title: A Fatal Triad of Myeloradiculitis, Multifocal Cerebral Infarction, and Central Retinal Artery Occlusion Revealing Occult Giant Cell Arteritis.
items.abstract: Giant cell arteritis (GCA) is the most common primary systemic vasculitis in adults over 50 years of age and classically presents with cranial symptoms such as headache, jaw claudication, and scalp tenderness. Spinal cord involvement is exceedingly rare and easily mistaken for degenerative spinal disease, particularly when headache, jaw claudication, and scalp tenderness are absent. We report the case of a 61-year-old woman whose illness evolved over several months, beginning with a lower-limb deficit and sciatica misdiagnosed as a disc herniation and treated surgically without improvement. Only when a contralateral deficit, a sensory level, and sphincter dysfunction emerged was a thoracic myeloradiculitis recognized on MRI. Days before admission, an acute monocular visual loss and a new upper-limb deficit revealed a more extensive process, and biopsy-confirmed GCA with large-vessel involvement and multifocal cerebral lesions was ultimately diagnosed. Despite an initial partial response to high-dose glucocorticoids, the patient died of septic shock before advanced imaging for disease-extent assessment could be performed, owing to local resource constraints. This case illustrates the diagnostic pitfalls of spinal-onset GCA without headache, jaw claudication, or scalp tenderness, and the infectious risk of high-dose glucocorticoid therapy in severe large-vessel disease.

items.title: An Atypical Case of Antineutrophil Cytoplasmic Antibody (ANCA)-Associated Vasculitis With Isolated Lower Airway Involvement in a Young Adult.
items.abstract: Antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)-associated vasculitides (AAV) typically present in middle-aged adults with multiorgan involvement. We describe the case of a 19-year-old woman with asthma, progressive dyspnea, and recurrent bronchial stenosis and webbing. Serological testing showed rising perinuclear ANCA (p-ANCA) and anti-myeloperoxidase (MPO) antibody titers, whereas cytoplasmic ANCA (c-ANCA) and anti-proteinase 3 (PR3) antibodies were negative. Biopsy revealed nonspecific inflammation and fibrosis. Infectious causes, malignancy, relapsing polychondritis, and sarcoidosis were excluded. Although the presentation did not meet the 2022 American College of Rheumatology/European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology (ACR/EULAR) classification criteria threshold for granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA), which are intended for research classification rather than clinical diagnosis, bronchial-limited AAV, most consistent with GPA, was considered the working diagnosis. The patient improved following corticosteroid treatment and bronchoscopic dilation.

items.title: Engineered pediatric human muscle models the interferon-driven transcriptome of juvenile dermatomyositis.
items.abstract: Juvenile dermatomyositis (JDM) is a rare pediatric autoimmune disease characterized by a strong type I interferon (IFN) signature in muscle. Mechanistic and therapeutic discovery has been limited by the lack of a clinically relevant disease model. To address this, we tested whether IFN treatment of a human muscle-derived microphysiological system (myobundles) recapitulates the transcriptional profile of JDM muscle. Principal component analysis of RNA sequencing from healthy and JDM muscle along with IFN-treated and untreated myobundles revealed separation of healthy and untreated samples from JDM and IFN-treated samples. JDM muscle exhibited 4,121 differentially expressed genes (DEGs, p adj <0.05) compared to healthy muscle, of which 56.2% showed concordant differential expression in IFNβ-treated and 30.0% in IFNα-treated myobundles. Hallmark pathway analysis demonstrated concordant directional changes between JDM muscle and IFN-treated myobundles. IFN and inflammatory pathways were most upregulated; oxidative phosphorylation, fatty acid metabolism, and adipogenesis were downregulated, though not reproducible across sites. Normalized enrichment score correlations between JDM muscle and IFN-treated myobundles were strongly positive ( r  = 0.63, p =1 × 10 - 6 for IFNα; r  = 0.67, p  = 1.3 × 10 - 7 for IFNβ). These findings indicate that IFN-treated myobundles, particularly with IFNβ, mirror key transcriptional features of JDM muscle and provide a needed muscle-centric platform to study IFN-driven mechanisms and therapeutic targets. The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-026-72125-6.

items.title: A study on the screening of potential biomarkers for rheumatoid arthritis based on nontarget metabolomics.
items.abstract: To explore changes in blood metabolites with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) using non-targeted metabolomics techniques, to identify potential metabolic biomarkers in RA patients. Twenty patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA group) who attended the Sichuan Province Orthopaedic Hospital between July and December 2023 were recruited, and twenty healthy controls were included. Serum candidate metabolites were analysed using ultra-performance liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (UPLC-MS). Variable Importance in Projection (VIP) value > 1 and p < 0.05 as criteria for identifying specific differentially expressed candidate metabolites. Differential candidate metabolites and associated pathways were annotated via the KEGG database, and diagnostic value was detected by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves. 579 metabolites were detected, and based on the screening criteria, 16 were identified as important differentially expressed candidate metabolites associated with RA. The 10 up-regulated metabolites included PC(16:1(9Z)/20:0), PC(20:1(11Z)/18:4(6Z,9Z,12Z,15Z)), Palmitoylcarnitine, 3-O-Sulfogalactosylceramide (d18:1/20:0), GPEtn(16:1/22:4), Sphinganine, 3-Methylindole, PC(16:1(9Z)/20:5(5Z,8Z,11Z,14Z,17Z)), Ortho-Hydroxyphenylacetic acid, PE(18:1(11Z)/18:3(9Z,12Z,15Z)). The 6 downregulated metabolites included PE-NMe(18:4(6Z,9Z,12Z,15Z)/18:4(6Z,9Z,12Z,15Z)), PE(22:0/15:0), PS(18:2(9Z,12Z)/22:4(7Z,10Z,13Z,16Z)), CDP-DG(a-13:0/i-12:0), 3a,7a,12a-Trihydroxy-5b-cholestan-26-al, and Serotonin. Using an area under the curve (AUC) of > 0.8 as a criterion, four potential biomarkers for RA were identified, including PE(22:0/15:0) (AUC = 0.8333, 95% CI: 0.6244-1), PE-NMe(18:4(6Z,9Z,12Z,15Z)/18:4(6Z,9Z,12Z,15Z))(AUC = 0.9722, 95% CI: 0.6571-1), Sphinganine (AUC = 0.9167, 95% CI: 0.7143-1), GPEtn(16:1/22:4)(AUC = 0.8889, 95% CI: 0.7429-1). The AUC for the combined diagnosis of RA using the four differentially expressed candidate metabolites was 0.961 (95% CI: 0.9463-0.9757). Glycerophospholipid metabolism was the most significantly altered pathway in RA, according to pathway enrichment analysis. Our research identified four potential biomarkers: PE(22:0/15:0), PE-NMe(18:4(6Z,9Z,12Z,15Z)/18:4(6Z,9Z,12Z,15Z)), Sphinganine, and GPEtn(16:1/22:4). Glycerophospholipid metabolism may be involved in RA. This study was entirely exploratory research and framed as hypothesis-generating only, which will require further validation in subsequent research.

items.title: Time course of the placebo response and associated factors in clinical trials of biologic agents for ankylosing spondylitis.
items.abstract: To characterize the time course and influencing factors of placebo response in randomized trials of biologic and targeted synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (tsDMARDs) for ankylosing spondylitis (AS). We systematically searched major electronic databases (up to June 14, 2024) for randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trials of biologics or Janus kinase inhibitors in AS. Model-based meta-analysis with nonlinear mixed-effects modeling was conducted to pool placebo-arm ASAS20 (≥20% improvement by Assessment of SpondyloArthritis International Society criteria) and ASAS40 (≥40% improvement) response trajectories, using an exponential rise-to-maximum model with covariate screening and model validation. Thirty-eight trial arms from 36 trials (3046 placebo-treated participants) were included. The estimated maximum response (P max ) was 31.1% for ASAS20 (90% of P max reached at 6.5 weeks) and 18.6% for ASAS40 (90% of P max reached at 17.0 weeks). ASAS20 P max increased by 2.7% per publication year. Smaller trials, no background therapy, lower male proportion, and lower baseline HLA-B27 positivity were associated with higher placebo response. The AS placebo response, particularly for ASAS20, shows a significant upward secular trend. This model provides a quantitative benchmark for trial design, anomalous placebo responses identification, and interpreting efficacy in trials lacking a concurrent placebo arm. Ankylosing spondylitis (AS) is a long-term inflammatory disease that mainly affects the joints of the spine. To find out whether a new medicine works, researchers compare it with a placebo, a dummy treatment with no active drug. The difficulty is that people given a placebo often improve anyway, and by very different amounts from trial to trial. When the placebo response is unusually large, an effective medicine can look as though it does not work. We collected data from 38 published AS trials of biologic medicines or Janus kinase inhibitors, covering 3046 people who received a placebo. Using a mathematical model, we described how the placebo response changes with time and what makes it larger or smaller. Two findings stood out. First, the placebo response grows slowly and then levels off: it takes about 6.5 weeks to reach its maximum when improvement reaches 20% and about 17 weeks when it reaches a stricter 40%, so a trial that stops early may underestimate the placebo group’s improvement. Second, the placebo response has grown by about 2.7% a year since 2002. It also tends to be larger in smaller trials, in trials where background painkillers were not allowed, in trials with fewer men and in trials where fewer patients carried the human leukocyte antigen B27 (HLA-B27) gene. Our model is a reference point: it helps researchers judge whether a new trial’s placebo response is unusually large or small, and interpret trials that had no placebo group. It may help design smaller, faster trials.

items.title: A machine learning-based predictive tool for complete renal response in lupus nephritis leverages the 3-month treatment milestone.
items.abstract: Lupus nephritis (LN) remains a major determinant of poor prognosis in systemic lupus erythematosus, yet reliable tools for early identification of unfavorable renal outcomes are lacking. This study aimed to identify early prognostic factors for complete renal response (CRR) at 12 months in active LN and to develop interpretable machine learning (ML) models for early prediction of treatment response. In this prospective cohort of 400 active LN patients followed for 12 months, the primary outcome was 12-month CRR. Candidate predictors were assessed at baseline and 3-month follow-up. Four ML models (Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, Elastic Net, and eXtreme Gradient Boosting) were developed and validated on a test set. Model performance was evaluated using area under the ROC curve (AUC), calibration and decision curve analyses, with feature importance assessed via SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). 296 patients (74%) achieved CRR at 12 months. Baseline factors independently associated with CRR included 24-hour urinary total protein (24hUTP), higher serum albumin, shorter disease duration, and treatment-naïve status. Significant group differences emerged at 3 months across multiple parameters (all p  < 0.05). Baseline‑only models showed limited discriminative ability (AUC ≤ 0.75), whereas incorporating 3-month data markedly improved performance; the Random Forest model achieved the best testing-set AUC (0.862, 95% CI: 0.775-0.949). SHAP analysis identified 3-month 24hUTP reduction as the most influential predictor of CRR. We developed an interpretable ML tool that accurately predicts 12-month CRR as early as 3 months post-treatment, highlighting the critical role of early proteinuria reduction as a key indicator for long-term renal outcomes.

items.title: Wearable interstitial fluid sensing of time-resolved uric acid for early prediction of flare-associated pain in an induced mouse model.
items.abstract: Gout flare is driven by hyperuricemia (HUA) and inflammatory responses to monosodium urate (MSU) crystals, yet single time-point serum uric acid (UA) measurements cannot capture the biochemical dynamics preceding flare onset or explain the timing of severe pain manifestation. Here, we present a skin-attachable interstitial fluid (ISF)-based electrochemical sensing platform for time-resolved, minimally invasive UA monitoring in a controlled, induced mouse model of gout flare-associated inflammation and pain. The platform integrates an enzyme-based UA sensor, a thin insertion electrode, and battery-free near-field communication (NFC), enabling time-resolved in vivo tracking of ISF UA dynamics. By establishing disease-stage-specific models comprising HUA, MSU-only inflammation, and gouty arthritis flare (GA flare) conditions, we separately examined metabolic and inflammatory contributions to flare-associated UA dynamics. Time-resolved ISF monitoring revealed that the GA flare group exhibited pronounced UA fluctuation patterns that were not reproduced by either condition alone. The peak timing of UA dynamics was temporally decoupled from pain-related behavioral responses, indicating that flare-associated pain onset cannot be explained by a single UA concentration. A machine learning framework using ISF UA time-series features identified predictive information preceding peak pain, whereas analyses using earlier events defined by sustained decreases in paw withdrawal threshold showed lower and event-definition-dependent performance. These findings establish time-resolved ISF UA monitoring as a framework for resolving flare-associated biochemical dynamics and evaluating subsequent pain progression in an induced mouse model.

items.title: Eosinophilic Granulomatosis with Polyangiitis: From Disease Heterogeneity to Phenotype-Driven Treatment.
items.abstract: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) is a heterogeneous disease in which eosinophilic inflammation, type 2 immunity, and antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)-associated vasculitis contribute to varying degrees among individual patients. The introduction of interleukin-5 (IL-5)/IL-5 receptor-targeted therapies, particularly mepolizumab and benralizumab, has transformed EGPA management, enabling substantial glucocorticoid (GC) reduction and making GC-free disease control achievable in selected patients. However, conventional immunosuppression remains important for severe organ-threatening disease, and optimal treatment selection requires consideration of disease severity, organ involvement, eosinophilic versus vasculitic manifestations, relapse pattern, and GC dependency. Major unmet needs include the optimal timing and selection of biologic therapy, strategies for GC withdrawal, and improved definitions of disease activity and remission. This review discusses recent therapeutic advances and proposes a phenotype-driven approach to treatment selection, while highlighting the future transition toward molecular endotyping and precision medicine.

items.title: Vasculitic myopathy as the initial manifestation of microscopic polyangiitis with sustained remission following rituximab induction and avacopan maintenance: a case report.
items.abstract: Microscopic polyangiitis (MPA), a form of antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)-associated vasculitis (AAV), can involve skeletal muscle. However, vasculitic myopathy remains underrecognized, and no consensus has been established regarding its optimal management. A 67-year-old Japanese man presented with progressive myalgia predominantly affecting the lower extremities. Laboratory evaluation revealed elevated inflammatory markers and myeloperoxidase-ANCA positivity, while serum creatine kinase levels remained within the normal range. Thigh magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) demonstrated diffuse hyperintensity on short tau inversion recovery sequences involving the quadriceps muscles. Muscle biopsy revealed inflammatory cell infiltration with fibrinoid necrosis in small vessels, confirming the diagnosis of vasculitic myopathy associated with MPA. Remission was achieved with induction therapy using glucocorticoids and rituximab, followed by maintenance therapy with avacopan. Subsequent MRI showed complete resolution of muscular abnormalities, and sustained clinical remission was maintained without relapse. This case demonstrates the utility of MRI for the early detection of MPA-associated vasculitic myopathy and for assessing treatment response, and suggests that avacopan may be a promising option for remission maintenance in this condition.

items.title: Classification and surgical treatment of temporomandibular joint calcium pyrophosphate deposition disease: a single-center case series.
items.abstract: This study aimed to classify calcium pyrophosphate deposition disease of the temporomandibular joint and evaluate the therapeutic outcomes. Surgically treated patients from January 2020 to September 2025 were classified into three types based on lesion location and extent. Type I involved the superior compartment with or without skull base destruction. Type II affected the inferior compartment with or without condylar destruction. Type III involved both compartments affecting the condyle and skull base. Treatments included complete excision and reconstruction using autologous or alloplastic materials. Maximum interincisal opening and visual analogue scale pain scores were evaluated preoperatively and at follow-ups of at least 6 months, while computed tomography assessed recurrence and reconstruction. Ten patients (mean age of 57.2 years) were included, comprising four in type I, four in type II, and two in type III. Bone invasion occurred in eight patients. Reconstruction procedures involved autologous tissues, such as temporalis myofascial flaps or coronoid grafts in three patients, and alloplastic materials in five. The mean follow-up duration was 25.1 months. Maximum (range) interincisal opening was improved from 33.0 mm (23.0-48.0) to 39.5 mm (37.0-45.0) (P < 0.05). Pain scores decreased from 6.0 (2.0-8.0) to 0.0 (0.0-1.0) (P < 0.05). One patient had coronoid process graft resorption without malocclusion. No recurrence, screw loosening, or implant displacement occurred. TMJ CPPD can be classified and treated according to the lesion location and extension. Complete excision and reconstruction are associated with low recurrence.

items.title: Treat-to-target strategies in juvenile systemic lupus erythematosus: A scoping review of current evidence and future directions.
items.abstract: Treat-to-target (T2T) has emerged as a promising strategy to potentially improve long-term outcomes in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). While T2T principles are well established in adult-onset disease, their adaptation to juvenile-onset SLE (jSLE) is more recent, with evidence remaining largely observational. To synthesise and map the current evidence, a systematic search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Ovid and Web of Science using terms related to jSLE, T2T, remission and Lupus Low Disease Activity State (LLDAS). Peer-reviewed English-language studies including patients diagnosed before age 18 were eligible if they addressed target development or validation, implementation strategies, associations with outcomes, facilitators or barriers to target attainment, biomarkers or lupus nephritis in the context of T2T. Reviews, editorials, conference abstracts, non-English publications and non-paediatric T2T studies were excluded. Of 347 identified records, 24 met inclusion criteria. These included work on target development and validation, implementation approaches and evaluation of clinical impact. Across studies, 67-100% of patients reached LLDAS or childhood LLDAS, 11-61% achieved remission on-steroids, and 2-31% achieved remission off-steroids, depending on definitions. Target attainment was consistently associated with fewer flares and less damage. Factors such as absence of renal disease, early use of mycophenolate mofetil and biologics supported target achievement, while African/Caribbean ethnicity, renal involvement, high disease activity at onset, and the glucocorticoid dose negatively influenced the likelihood of reaching targets. Although evidence is growing, variability in target definitions and study design limits comparability. Paediatric-specific targets represent an important step forward, with priorities now including validation, biomarker integration and prospective evaluation in a clinical trial.

items.title: Beyond clinical remission in rheumatoid arthritis: Lessons from hematology and gastroenterology.
items.abstract: Treat-to-target strategies have substantially improved outcomes in rheumatoid arthritis (RA), yet current remission definitions rely largely on clinical composite criteria and may not fully reflect underlying inflammatory activity. Deep remission is not new in RA, and previous studies have used the term to describe increasingly stringent clinical, imaging, or immunological states. However, these definitions remain heterogeneous, and the clinical significance and actionability of remission depth remain uncertain. Drawing on lessons from chronic myeloid leukemia and inflammatory bowel disease, we reappraise deep remission in RA as a multidimensional concept rather than a new hierarchical treatment target. Clinical remission remains the established treatment target, while imaging and immunological assessments may provide complementary information on residual disease activity. Negative imaging-guided strategy trials do not support treatment escalation solely to achieve imaging normalization, but leave open whether objective phenotyping beyond clinical remission offers broader prognostic and clinical value. We synthesize evidence on whether deep remission assessments provide incremental prognostic or clinically actionable information for structural progression, remission durability, treatment tapering or withdrawal, sustained drug-free remission in selected patients, and cardiovascular outcomes. Deep remission may therefore serve as an aspirational direction for RA care, not as a mandate to normalize every residual abnormality, but as a broader goal of achieving durable, biology-informed control, with the potential to support safer treatment de-escalation in selected patients.

items.title: Ocular phenotypes of Sjogren's disease based on light sensitivity: A pilot study on differences in sub-basal corneal nerve plexus, tear cytokines, and neuropeptides.
items.abstract: To evaluate whether individuals with Sjögren's disease (SjD) and light sensitivity differ in corneal nerve morphology, tear cytokines, or neuropeptide profiles from those with SjD without light sensitivity and with controls. This pilot, cross-sectional study conducted at a tertiary eye hospital in India included SjD patients with (n=10, defined as a "yes" response to light-induced or light-exacerbated ocular pain) and without light sensitivity (n=10; satisfied ACR/EULAR 2016 criteria; not on topical antiinflammatory), and age- and sex-matched healthy controls (n=9). Groups were compared for Ocular Surface Disease Index (OSDI), tear film parameters, ocular surface staining, symptom-sign alignment, mechanical corneal sensitivity, in-vivo confocal microscopy, tear cytokines, and neuropeptides. The two SjD groups were similar with respect to demographics, OSDI scores (excluding light sensitivity item), tear film parameters, symptom-sign alignment, and corneal nerve metrics. However, SjD with light sensitivity exhibited reduced mechanical corneal sensitivity (38.5 ± 11.1 vs. 54 ± 2.1 mm; p = 0.0006), decreased mature dendritic cell density (3 ± 4 vs. 7.7 ± 4.6 cells/mm 2 ; p = 0.04), and lower levels of inflammatory cytokines (IL-17, IL-13, IL-10, and IL-5), compared with SjD without light sensitivity. Compared with controls, both SjD groups had significantly higher symptom severity, abnormal tear parameters, and a more inflammatory ocular surface profile. The findings of reduced mechanical sensitivity and less ocular surface inflammation in the SjD with light sensitivity group suggest different SjD clinical phenotypes, potentially distinguishing those with a greater contribution of altered sensory processing from those with predominantly ocular surface-driven inflammatory disease.

items.title: Compartment-specific complement dysregulation in lupus nephritis: Associations with disease activity and response to therapy.
items.abstract: Lupus nephritis (LN) is a severe manifestation of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) in which serum C3 and C4 often fail to reflect local renal complement activation. We assessed compartment-specific complement activation in paired serum and urine as a non-invasive biomarker of LN activity and treatment response. Complement proteins Ba, Bb, C3a, C4a, C5a, sC5b-9, factor H, and factor I were measured by multiplex assay in paired serum and urine samples from 21 patients with LN with kidney biopsy before and one year after initiation of therapy, 20 LN-naïve SLE patients, and 15 healthy controls (HC). Serum levels were normalised to mean HC. Urine levels in the LN cohort were normalised to urine creatinine; between-group comparisons used raw urinary concentrations. Active LN patients exhibited higher serum C4a and sC5b-9 but lower factors H and I compared to LN-naïve SLE patients. Urine levels of all measured complement proteins were elevated in LN patients relative to LN-naïve SLE patients and HC. Following one year of immunosuppressive therapy, serum Ba, Bb, C5a, sC5b-9, factors H and I declined significantly, as did urinary Ba and C5a. LN patients achieving clinical response at one year had higher baseline urinary Bb, C3a, C4a, factors H and I than non-responders; these differences remained significant after correction across the eight urinary analytes. In this exploratory study, serum and urinary complement profiles provided distinct yet complementary information in LN. Complement levels declined following one year of immunosuppressive therapy, and baseline urinary complement profiling showed associations with treatment outcome, warranting validation in larger independent cohorts.
