items.title: Current perspectives on the pharmacotherapeutic management of rheumatoid arthritis-associated lung disease.
items.abstract: Pulmonary involvement affects approximately 30-40% of patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA). Although interstitial lung disease (ILD) has received the greatest attention, non-ILD pulmonary manifestations also contribute substantially to respiratory morbidity. Biologic therapies in RA have improved disease outcomes however, their use in RA-associated lung disease remains challenging due to limited high-quality data. This narrative review summarizes current evidence on the pharmacotherapeutic management of RA-associated lung disease, across its spectrum, focusing on ILD. A literature search was performed in PudmMed/Medline, Scopus and the Directory of Open Access Journals databases up to August 2026. Early recognition of RA-associated lung disease is crucial, therefore close follow-up and monitoring are mandatory. Pharmacotherapy requires an individualized strategy, rather than the one-size-fits-all. Corticosteroids may be considered in RA-associated ILD (RA-ILD) patients with an inflammatory imaging pattern or non-ILD manifestations (e.g. airway and pleural disease), although prolonged use should generally be avoided. Methotrexate (MTX) can be continued in RA-ILD patients, unless MTX-induced pneumonitis is suspected. Immunomodulatory agents may stabilize lung function, whereas antifibrotics offer the strongest trial-based evidence, especially in individuals with usual interstitial pneumonia or with progressive disease. High-quality prospective studies are needed. Until then, multidisciplinary, personalized approach should be followed.

items.title: Colchicine use was associated with reduced all-cause mortality in patients with diabetic gout without prior coronary artery disease: A propensity-matched nationwide cohort study.
items.abstract: Colchicine has been associated with reduced cardiovascular events in secondary prevention, but evidence for primary prevention is limited. We examined the association between colchicine use and cardiovascular outcomes in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus and gout without prior coronary artery disease. From the Korean National Health Insurance Service database, we identified 48,295 patients with diabetes and gout without prior coronary artery disease between 2015 and 2019. We compared 28,964 colchicine users with 19,331 non-users by 1:1 propensity score matching, which produced 17,337 matched pairs. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, and nonfatal stroke. The primary composite outcome occurred in 12.52% of colchicine users versus 15.03% of non-users (hazard ratio [HR] 0.71; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.66-0.75; P < 0.001). All-cause mortality was significantly reduced in colchicine users (8.01% vs. 11.07%; HR 0.58; 95% CI 0.53-0.62; P < 0.001). No significant differences were observed for myocardial infarction (HR 1.15; 95% CI 0.96-1.37; P = 0.121) or stroke (HR 0.91; 95% CI 0.81-1.01; P = 0.076). In a landmark analysis at 365 days that addressed immortal time bias, the associations with all-cause mortality (HR 0.67; 95% CI 0.62-0.73; P < 0.001) and with the composite outcome (HR 0.76; 95% CI 0.71-0.81; P < 0.001) remained significant, whereas stroke (HR 0.99; 95% CI 0.87-1.12; P = 0.823) and myocardial infarction (HR 1.15; 95% CI 0.95-1.40; P = 0.144) did not differ between the two groups. In patients with diabetes and gout without prior coronary artery disease, colchicine use was associated with lower all-cause mortality. The reduction in the composite outcome was driven by mortality rather than by myocardial infarction or stroke.

items.title: Allergen-Specific Antibodies Dysregulation and Profiles in IgG4-Related Disease: A Hybrid Case-Control and Cross-Sectional Study.
items.abstract: Although patients with immunoglobulin-G4-related disease (IgG4-RD) frequently have comorbid allergic diseases, the specific allergen-specific antibody profiles and their association with distinct organ-involvement phenotypes remain unclear. We conducted a hybrid study with 208 patients with IgG4-RD and 104 age- and sex-matched general population controls (controls). A case-control approach was used to compare the allergen-specific antibody profiles between patients and controls. Within the IgG4-RD cohort, a cross-sectional analysis was performed by utilizing K-modes clustering to identify organ-involvement phenotypes; multivariate logistic regression was used to assess independent associations between antibody patterns and these phenotypes. Compared with controls, patients with IgG4-RD had significantly reduced sIgG4 levels against house-dust-mite (HDM) components and elevated sIgE/sIgG4 ratios, which suggested a breakdown in immune tolerance. Within the IgG4-RD cohort, three distinct organ phenotypes were identified. Multivariate analysis revealed that a pattern of high concurrent sIgE and sIgG4 responses to Der p 5 and Der p 21 was strongly associated with the exocrine gland-involvement phenotype (OR = 906.70, p = 0.003), whereas an IgE-dominant pattern against food allergens was inversely associated with this phenotype (OR = 0.16, p = 0.016). The shift in the sIgE/sIgG4 balance suggests that impaired allergen-specific immune tolerance is closely linked to IgG4-RD clinical heterogeneity. Distinct antibody patterns, specifically a dual IgE/IgG4 response to Der p 5 and Der p 21, were independently associated with exocrine gland involvement. Thus, allergen-specific profiling constitutes a valuable tool for characterizing disease phenotypes and investigating the underlying pathomechanisms.

items.title: Incidence of Cancer in Morphea and Systemic Sclerosis.
items.abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is associated with increased risk of cancer, but population-level data on cancer risk in morphea remain limited and conflicting. To compare the incidence and standardized incidence ratios (SIRs) of overall and site-specific cancers in patients with morphea and SSc compared with the general population, and to identify factors associated with incident cancer. This is a retrospective, population-based cohort study using linked administrative health databases (1996-2019) from Quebec, Canada, with follow-up through December 31, 2020. Patients were identified using published diagnostic algorithms requiring at least 2 billing claims with relevant International Classification of Diseases, Ninth Revision, and/or International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, Tenth Revision, codes at least 2 months apart, with specialist diagnosis or hospitalization. Data were analyzed from June 2025 to June 2026. Diagnosis of morphea or SSc. Incident cancers were ascertained through linkage to the provincial cancer registry. SIRs were calculated with respect to the general population using Canadian Cancer Registry rates. Cumulative incidence was estimated using Fine-Gray competing risk methods; associated factors were evaluated with multivariable Cox regression. There were 6181 patients with morphea (median [IQR] age at diagnosis, 56 [40-68] years; 4605 female [74.50%]; 71 221.53 person-years of follow-up) and 8133 patients with SSc (median [IQR] age at diagnosis, 58 [48-69] years; 6530 female [80.29%]; 71 844.36 person-years of follow-up). During follow-up, 782 patients with morphea (12.65%) and 1104 with SSc (13.57%) developed cancer. Overall cancer incidence was increased in both the morphea (SIR, 1.24; 95% CI, 1.14-1.35) and SSc (SIR, 1.37; 95% CI, 1.27-1.48) cohorts. Solid tumor risk was elevated in both cohorts (morphea SIR, 1.17; 95% CI, 1.06-1.29; SSc SIR, 1.21; 95% CI 1.11-1.32). Hematologic cancer risk was markedly elevated in patients with SSc (SIR, 2.40; 95% CI, 1.92-2.96) but not statistically significant for those with morphea (SIR, 1.34; 95% CI, 0.97-1.81). Female reproductive and breast cancers predominated in the morphea group; lung cancer was most frequent among patients with SSc. Younger patients carried the highest relative risk. Immunosuppressant use was associated with lower cancer risk in patients with morphea (hazard ratio, 0.56; 95% CI, 0.46-0.68) and those with SSc (hazard ratio, 0.63; 95% CI, 0.55-0.70). This cohort study found that morphea and SSc were associated with increased cancer incidence compared with the general population, with distinct cancer profiles between the 2 conditions. These findings identify patients with morphea, like those with SSc, as a population warranting oncologic attention; whether disease-specific or intensified screening is beneficial requires further study.

items.title: Biomimetic Platelet Membrane-Coated PLGA Nanoparticles for Enhanced Zingerone Delivery in Experimental Rheumatoid Arthritis.
items.abstract: To develop and evaluate platelet membrane-coated poly (lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) nanoparticles encapsulating zingerone for targeted delivery and enhanced therapeutic efficacy against experimental rheumatoid arthritis. Rheumatoid arthritis is a chronic inflammatory disorder characterized by synovial inflammation, oxidative stress, and progressive cartilage and bone destruction, resulting in pain, disability, and impaired mobility. Existing therapies often provide incomplete disease control and may cause systemic adverse effects, necessitating the development of safer and more effective targeted treatment strategies. Zingerone-loaded PLGA nanoparticles were prepared and coated with platelet membranes to improve targeting of inflamed tissues. Physicochemical characterization included particle size, zeta potential, transmission electron microscopy, and spectroscopic analyses. Therapeutic efficacy was assessed in Freund's complete adjuvant-induced arthritic rats using clinical evaluation, cytokine quantification, antioxidant assessment, histopathology, radiography, and toxicity studies. Optimized ZP nanoparticles exhibited a mean hydrodynamic diameter of 134.35 ± 52.21 nm, which increased to 148.88 ± 69.35 nm following platelet membrane coating (PZP), indicating successful surface modification. Transmission electron microscopy demonstrated a spherical core-shell morphology, while spectroscopic analyses confirmed successful encapsulation without evidence of chemical incompatibility. Entrapment efficiency was 81.0 ± 1.0% for ZP and 81.7 ± 0.6% for PZP. Treatment significantly reduced paw edema (P < 0.001), arthritis scores, TNF-α, and IL-1β (P < 0.05), improved antioxidant status, preserved joint architecture, and produced no significant hepatic or renal toxicity. Platelet membrane-coated PLGA nanoparticles effectively enhanced zingerone delivery and anti-inflammatory activity, demonstrating considerable potential as a targeted nanotherapeutic platform for the management of rheumatoid arthritis.

items.title: Durable and Additive Disease Control at 52 Weeks With Ixekizumab Plus Tirzepatide Versus Ixekizumab Alone in Adults With Psoriatic Arthritis and Obesity or Overweight: Additional Results From a Randomized Clinical Trial.
items.abstract: Obesity or overweight occurs in 72% to 82% of individuals with psoriatic arthritis (PsA). Previous data revealed greater disease control with concomitant ixekizumab (IXE) and tirzepatide (TZP) versus IXE alone in adults with active PsA and obesity or overweight with at least one weight-related comorbidity at the week 36 primary end point. The objective of this report is to evaluate the effect of IXE+TZP versus IXE on psoriatic disease control and safety measures up to week 52. TOGETHER-PsA (ClinicalTrials.gov ID NCT06588296) is a phase 3b, randomized, open-label, assessor-blinded 52-week trial. Participants were randomized 1:1 to IXE+TZP or IXE using US-approved doses. Week 52 outcomes were prespecified, non-multiplicity-controlled, and exploratory. Outcomes included 50% improvement in American College of Rheumatology response criteria (ACR50) and rheumatologic, dermatologic, patient-reported, metabolic, and safety outcomes. A total of 271 participants were randomized (IXE+TZP, n = 138; IXE, n = 133). The proportion achieving the primary outcome of simultaneous ACR50 and ≥10% weight reduction continued to increase from week 36 through week 52 for IXE+TZP (39.2%) versus IXE (1.7%) (Δ37.5%; P < 0.001). ACR50 continued to diverge after week 36, with a clinically meaningful difference at week 52 for IXE+TZP (43.7%) versus IXE (15.7%) (Δ 28.0%; P < 0.001). IXE+TZP demonstrated significant improvements in ACR20, minimal disease activity, Disease Activity Index for Psoriatic Arthritis, patient-reported outcomes, and metabolic outcomes versus IXE alone. Safety profiles were consistent with previous studies for each drug. Comprehensive improvements in disease activity, including ACR50, quality of life, weight, and metabolic outcomes, continued through week 52 and were greater with IXE+TZP than IXE alone, with no new safety concerns. These findings support concomitant IXE+TZP in patients with active PsA and immunometabolic disease.

items.title: Scoping Review of Human Longitudinal Studies of Biomarkers Associated with Risk of Developing Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) to Inform the Development of a Novel SLE Risk Stratification Index.
items.abstract: SLE is often preceded by a preclinical phase in which autoantibodies and other biomarkers are detectable, offering an opportunity to identify at-risk individuals for early monitoring and testing interventions to halt progression. To inform an effort to develop SLE risk-stratification criteria, we conducted a scoping review of longitudinal human studies of biomarkers measured before SLE onset. Following PRISMA-ScR, we searched three databases and used a Population, Exposure, Comparator, Outcome framework to select longitudinal studies in which biomarkers were measured before an incident diagnosis or classification of SLE. Study characteristics, biomarkers, and outcomes were extracted from included studies. We included 59 original studies and two meta-analyses including heterogeneous at-risk populations, in which the proportion progressing to SLE varied widely. Most evidence concerned conventional serological markers, whereas interferon and cytokine signatures, proteomic panels, and genetic risk scores were examined in fewer, recent cohorts. Few biomarkers were studied across multiple populations or with comparable follow-up, outcome definitions, and analytic methods, and most associations came from single studies without external validation. Longitudinal biomarker trajectories before onset were rarely characterized, and non-European populations were under-represented. his review maps the breadth of candidate biomarkers associated with the risk of developing SLE and the heterogeneity of the evidence supporting them. Building a clinically useful SLE risk-stratification index will need a shared definition of the at-risk state, and prospective studies that follow biomarkers over time, in populations from broader geographical regions.

items.title: Chronic Calcific Pancreatitis as the Probable Initial Manifestation of Systemic Lupus Erythematosus With Mixed Connective Tissue Disease Overlap: A Case Report.
items.abstract: Chronic calcific pancreatitis as the presenting manifestation of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is exceedingly rare, particularly in tropical regions where it may be misattributed to tropical chronic pancreatitis (TCP). A 22-year-old Bangladeshi male farmer presented with a one-year history of recurrent postprandial epigastric pain and steatorrhea. Three months before admission, he developed inflammatory polyarthritis, a photosensitive malar rash, oral ulcers, Raynaud phenomenon, and progressive proximal muscle weakness. Investigations revealed normocytic anemia (hemoglobin 9.2 g/dL), thrombocytopenia (50 × 10 9 /L), a positive direct Coombs test, and a broad autoantibody profile including strongly positive antinuclear antibodies, anti-dsDNA, anti-U1-RNP, anti-nucleosome, anti-Ku, and anti-ribosomal P antibodies. Computed tomography and magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography showed chronic calcific pancreatitis with beaded main pancreatic duct dilatation (10-11 mm), diffuse intraductal calculi, and parenchymal atrophy, without features of autoimmune pancreatitis. He fulfilled the 2019 EULAR/ACR classification criteria for SLE (score 22) and the Sharp criteria for mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD) overlap. Alcohol use, gallstone disease, hypercalcemia, hypertriglyceridemia, pancreatotoxic drugs, and cassava exposure were absent, but genetic testing and serum IgG4 were unavailable. Hydroxychloroquine, prednisolone, mycophenolate mofetil, and pancreatic enzyme replacement were followed by improvement of the systemic features, including platelet normalization. On the available evidence, the pancreatic disease is most plausibly an early manifestation of SLE-MCTD overlap, although a hereditary or tropical contribution cannot be formally excluded. This case expands the spectrum of SLE-associated pancreatic disease and underscores the need for systematic autoimmune evaluation in young patients from tropical regions with unexplained chronic calcific pancreatitis.

items.title: Rheumatoid Arthritis and Thrombocytopenia: Causal Evidence and Prognostic Implications From Observational and Mendelian Randomization Analyzes.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a systemic autoimmune disease associated with hematological abnormalities, and we aimed to investigate the clinical significance and causal relationship of thrombocytopenia (TP) in RA. We integrated observational data with genetic approaches, characterized the clinical features of RA patients with TP, and evaluated their prognostic implications. Data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey were used to analyze clinical characteristics and survival outcomes of RA patients. Survey-weighted Cox regression models were applied to evaluate the association between TP and mortality. Two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis was performed to evaluate the causal relationship between RA and TP. Among 2667 RA participants with available platelet measurements, 135 had TP (< 150 × 10 9 /L). In the common complete-case sample, TP remained associated with higher all-cause mortality after full survey-weighted adjustment (HR 1.92, 95% CI 1.17-3.16; p = 0.009). Lower serum albumin and higher urinary albumin concentration were also associated with mortality in the fully adjusted model. In the MR analysis using 52 SNPs, fixed-effect IVW yielded OR 1.054 (95% CI 1.002-1.108; p = 0.042), but alternative estimators were not significant and the MR-Egger intercept indicated directional pleiotropy (p = 0.0016). Thrombocytopenia was associated with poorer survival among RA participants, whereas MR did not provide robust evidence for a causal effect of RA liability on thrombocytopenia. These findings warrant further prospective validation.

items.title: Anti-MDA5 antibody-positive dermatomyositis complicated by unilateral vocal cord paralysis: A case report.
items.abstract: Hoarseness is a well-recognized feature in patients with anti-melanoma differentiation-associated protein 5 antibody-positive dermatomyositis (MDA5-DM); however, vocal cord paralysis (VCP) is a distinctly uncommon complication. To date, VCP has been rarely reported in MDA5-DM or other inflammatory myopathies, and the limited published cases have described exclusively bilateral cord involvement; unilateral VCP has not been documented. Although Janus kinase inhibitors have shown some effectiveness in treating refractory MDA5-DM, their therapeutic role in VCP remains unclear. A 47-year-old Chinese woman with MDA5-DM had clinical improvement after treatment with glucocorticoids and cyclosporine; then she was discharged. However, 2 day after discharge, she experienced a sudden onset of hoarseness, difficulty swallowing liquids, chest tightness, and shortness of breath. Flexible laryngoscopy showed immobility of the left vocal cord, consistent with left VCP. After ruling out causes such as neck surgery, trauma, and mechanical compression, we determined that the unilateral recurrent laryngeal nerve injury was related to MDA5-DM. Because of severe gingival hyperplasia and worsening hoarseness, cyclosporine was discontinued and replaced with tacrolimus. Tofacitinib was added, along with voice therapy. By day 13, the patient's hoarseness and choking had improved substantially; by day 20, these symptoms had resolved completely. Unilateral VCP may represent a rare neurological complication in patients with MDA5-DM. For patients who present with hoarseness, difficulty swallowing liquids, or unexplained worsening of shortness of breath, laryngoscopy should be considered to facilitate early diagnosis. If calcineurin inhibitors are not tolerated or the response is inadequate, adding a Janus kinase inhibitor such as tofacitinib may be considered as part of a comprehensive immunosuppressive regimen; however, because multiple interventions were used concurrently in this case, the independent contribution of tofacitinib to neurological recovery could not be determined.

items.title: Uncovering metabolite-inflammatory protein interactions in gout pathogenesis: A 2-sample bidirectional Mendelian randomization study.
items.abstract: Gout is a widespread inflammatory arthritis whose current treatments focus mainly on symptom relief and urate lowering. Recent work suggests that circulating metabolites and inflammatory proteins interact in complex ways to influence disease risk, with fibroblast growth factor 19 (FGF19) standing out as a potential regulatory node linking metabolism and inflammation. We performed bidirectional 2-sample Mendelian randomization using genome-wide association study summary statistics for 1440 serum metabolites and 91 inflammatory proteins, with gout outcomes drawn from FinnGen R12. Mediation analyses were then applied to examine whether FGF19 acts as an intermediary in selected metabolite-gout pathways. Genetically predicted levels of vanillactate and histidine betaine were associated with higher gout risk, whereas sphingomyelin species and taurolithocholate 3-sulfate showed protective effects. Among inflammatory proteins, FGF19, adenosine deaminase and FGF5 appeared protective, while cluster of differentiation 244 increased risk. Bidirectional analyses revealed reciprocal relationships, including a negative causal effect of propionylcarnitine on FGF19. Mediation testing further showed that FGF19 explained 7.88% of the total effect of lipid-related metabolites on gout via glycodeoxycholate 3-sulfate and 9.58% via cis-3,4-methyleneheptanoylglycine. These findings indicate that FGF19 may exert protective effects against gout partly by modulating bile acid and fatty acid metabolism. The results offer genetic evidence for metabolic-immune crosstalk in gout pathogenesis and highlight FGF19-related pathways as possible targets for more precise therapeutic strategies.

items.title: Intravascular large B-cell lymphoma presenting as unilateral lymphedema in a patient with rheumatoid arthritis and sarcoidosis: A case report.
items.abstract: Intravascular large B-cell lymphoma (IVLBCL) is an uncommon subtype of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, typically presenting with nonspecific symptoms and lacking lymphadenopathy or visible tumor lesions, which makes early diagnosis challenging. A 66-year-old female developed progressive unilateral lymphedema despite ongoing treatment for rheumatoid arthritis and sarcoidosis. Sarcoidosis-related lymph node lesions were also considered as a potential cause, and the prednisolone dose was increased. Despite these measures, the edema worsened, and a fever of around 38°C developed. At the initial evaluation, the serum soluble interleukin-2 receptor level was already elevated at 9985 U/mL. Initial investigations, including imaging, bone marrow aspiration, and random skin biopsies, failed to reveal malignancy. Subsequent monitoring revealed that the serum level of serum soluble interleukin-2 receptor had risen further to 19,835 U/mL and that thrombocytopenia was present, prompting a repeat random skin biopsy that ultimately confirmed IVLBCL through the identification of intravascular cluster of differentiation 20-positive lymphoma cells. Chemotherapy with rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, and prednisone was initiated. However, the patient developed peripheral neuropathy, suspected to be an adverse drug reaction. Consequently, the regimen was switched to polatuzumab vedotin, rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, and prednisolone. After completing 8 courses, the patient achieved remission. The left lower-limb lymphedema improved significantly. This case highlights several clinically significant points: first, IVLBCL can present solely as unilateral lymphedema without detectable lymph node enlargement or tumorous lesions, underscoring the diagnostic difficulty. Second, repeated random skin biopsies, including adipose-rich vascular tissue, are crucial in establishing a definitive diagnosis when initial biopsies are inconclusive. Third, patients with underlying autoimmune conditions such as rheumatoid arthritis and sarcoidosis, particularly those receiving immunosuppressive therapies, may have an increased susceptibility to lymphoma, suggesting that systemic immune dysregulation could contribute to disease onset.

items.title: Association of 14 matrix metalloproteinases and 4 tissue inhibitors of metalloproteinases on ankylosing spondylitis: A bidirectional Mendelian randomization study.
items.abstract: Observational studies link matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs) and tissue inhibitors of metalloproteinases (TIMPs) to ankylosing spondylitis (AS), but causality is uncertain. We performed a bidirectional, 2-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis using genetic variants to assess causal relationships between genetically predicted circulating levels of 14 MMPs and 4 TIMPs and AS risk, and to evaluate reverse causation. Genetic instruments for circulating MMPs and TIMPs were derived from a large proteogenomic genome-wide association study of 5368 individuals. Summary statistics for AS were obtained from the FinnGen Release 12 GWAS (3838 cases; 353,224 controls). Causal estimates were generated using inverse-variance weighting (primary analysis), complemented by MR-Egger, weighted median, and weighted mode methods. Sensitivity analyses included Cochran's Q test, MR-Egger intercept, MR-PRESSO, and leave-one-out analyses. Forward MR identified a nominal association between genetically predicted higher circulating MMP13 levels and an increased risk of AS (IVW odds ratio = 1.223, 95% confidence interval, 1.048-1.428; P = .011, FDR = 0.198). This association showed a consistent direction in the weighted median estimates and showed no evidence of heterogeneity or horizontal pleiotropy. No other MMPs or TIMPs showed convincing evidence of an association with AS. Reverse MR analyses provided no evidence that genetic liability to AS causally influences circulating MMP or TIMP levels. This bidirectional MR analysis provides genetic support for a potential causal relationship between MMP13 and the development of AS, while suggesting that other MMPs and TIMPs are unlikely to be causal drivers. Further experimental and clinical studies are warranted to clarify the biological relevance of MMP13 in AS.

items.title: Anti-SRP and anti-HMGCR co-positivity in immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy with interstitial lung disease: A rare case report.
items.abstract: Immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy (IMNM) is a rare inflammatory myopathy. Coexisting anti-signal recognition particle (anti-SRP) and anti-3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-coenzyme A reductase (anti-HMGCR) antibodies in statin-naïve patients with interstitial lung disease are exceptionally uncommon. A 55-year-old statin-naïve man presented with progressive proximal muscle weakness, dysphagia, myalgia, significant weight loss, and exertional dyspnea. Serum creatine kinase was 8000 U/L. Anti-SRP, anti-HMGCR, and anti-Ro52 antibodies were positive. Chest computed tomography showed bilateral consolidations and ground-glass opacities suggestive of organizing pneumonia. Pulmonary function tests revealed reduced forced vital capacity (52%) and diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide (48%). Electromyography and muscle biopsy findings supported IMNM. Treatment included high-dose corticosteroids, mycophenolate mofetil, nutritional support, and rehabilitation. After 3 months, muscle strength improved from 3/5 to 4+/5, dysphagia resolved, and weight increased by 5 kg. Creatine kinase decreased to 350 U/L, forced vital capacity improved to 74%, and diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide to 65%. Follow-up high-resolution computed tomography showed pulmonary improvement without fibrosis. This case highlights the rare coexistence of anti-SRP and anti-HMGCR antibodies in statin-naïve IMNM with interstitial lung disease. Early immunosuppression, nutritional support, and rehabilitation may improve muscular and pulmonary outcomes. Comprehensive respiratory assessment and longitudinal monitoring are essential.

items.title: Juvenile idiopathic arthritis and rheumatoid arthritis: a narrative review of age-dependent, subtype-specific immune mechanisms, biomarkers, and treatment strategies.
items.abstract: Juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) and adult rheumatoid arthritis (RA) share chronic inflammatory arthritis, but their biological drivers and implications vary by developmental stage and phenotype. JIA arises during immune and skeletal maturation and encompasses heterogeneous conditions, whereas adult RA develops after skeletal maturity. Existing reviews have considered the diseases separately or focused on polyarticular JIA, leaving uncertain which adult RA-derived mechanisms, biomarkers, and treatment principles transfer to JIA phenotypes. A targeted search of PubMed/MEDLINE and Web of Science through 25 September 2026 informed an age-by-endotype framework comparing JIA phenotypes with adult RA across immune and tissue mechanisms, structural consequences, biomarker function and evidence maturity, and treatment mechanism, exposure, and safety. Systemic JIA, conceptualized within the Still's disease spectrum, diverges most from adult RA because of myeloid-cell activation, macrophage activation syndrome risk, and inflammation associated with interleukin-1, interleukin-6, and interleukin-18. Rheumatoid factor (RF)-positive polyarticular JIA shows partial convergence with adult seropositive RA through autoantibody-associated adaptive immunity, chronic synovitis, and erosive potential, but development and pediatric safety preclude equivalence. Oligoarticular JIA is distinguished by synovitis and uveitis, whereas enthesitis-related arthritis and juvenile psoriatic arthritis align more closely with entheseal and psoriatic-spectrum biology than with RA. Biomarker interpretation and treatment are phenotype-specific: ferritin, interleukin-18, and S100 proteins inform systemic hyperinflammation; RF and anti-citrullinated protein antibodies characterize RA-like polyarthritis; antinuclear antibodies inform uveitis surveillance; and human leukocyte antigen B27 supports classification in enthesitis-related arthritis. Treatment ranges from early interleukin-1 or interleukin-6 inhibition in systemic JIA to methotrexate, biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs, and selected Janus kinase inhibitor use in RA-like polyarthritis after consideration of regulatory approval and individualized risk, and therapy directed at tumor necrosis factor or interleukin-17 in entheseal or psoriatic disease. Tissue, imaging, multi-omic, microbiome, and treatment-response biomarkers remain investigational. The relationship between JIA and adult RA is phenotype- and domain-specific rather than universal. This framework identifies where adult-derived evidence can inform pediatric interpretation and where direct pediatric validation is required. Longitudinal, subtype-defined pediatric cohorts integrating tissue, imaging, and multi-omic data are needed to support mechanism-based, developmentally appropriate care.

items.title: Triple-Positive Antiphospholipid Syndrome with Splenic Infarction Triggered by Tocilizumab Withdrawal in A High-Titer ACPA-Positive Rheumatoid Arthritis Patient: An Unmasking Storm of Polyautoimmunity.
items.abstract: We describe the occurrence of an uncommon thrombotic event, namely splenic infarction, as the onset of antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) after temporary suspension of anti-IL-6 treatment in a patient with rheumatoid arthritis (RA). A 53-year-old patient with anti-citrullinated protein antibody (ACPA) and rheumatoid factor-positive RA, previously showing transient positivity for immunoglobulin (Ig)G anticardiolipin antibodies and lupus anticoagulant (LAC), refractory to multiple biological disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs (DMARDs), anti-tumour necrosis factor (TNF)-α agents, and rituximab, had been treated with tocilizumab since 2013 with good clinical response. After temporary suspension of tocilizumab for minor orthopaedic surgery complicated by skin abscess, he developed acute abdominal pain and computed tomography evidence of splenic infarction. Laboratory evaluation revealed elevated inflammatory markers and triple positivity for LAC, aCL IgG, and aB2GPI IgG, leading to the diagnosis of APS. Treatment with warfarin, methotrexate, and baricitinib resulted in stable disease control without recurrent thrombotic events. Clinical stability in RA is a delicate balance between control of inflammation and avoidance of medication toxicity, especially in patients with high thrombotic risk and previous antiphospholipid positivity. Temporary withdrawal of biologic therapy may induce immunological rebound and thrombotic complications. This case highlights the importance of thrombotic risk stratification and multidisciplinary management when biologic therapies are suspended. Tocilizumab may act as a suppressor of autoreactive B-cell clones producing antiphospholipid antibodies.A high anti-citrullinated protein antibody (ACPA) titer may be associated with an increased risk of developing autoantibody storm with possible prothrombotic complications in rheumatoid arthritis, such as antiphospholipid syndrome.In case of surgical interventions in patients with rheumatoid arthritis treated with biological disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs (bDMARDs) it is important to evaluate the stratification of thrombotic risk with multidisciplinary discussion before suspending therapy.

items.title: [Behçet's syndrome as a rare cause of mucosal lesions and systemic symptoms in a young patient].
items.abstract: Behçet's syndrome is a rare systemic inflammatory disease. In Europe, it primarily affects individuals from families with a background in endemic regions. The disease is characterized by multisystem involvement, including mucocutaneous ulcerations, arthritis, and systemic symptoms that may mimic infectious or other autoimmune conditions. This case report presents a young male patient with fever, oral and genital ulcers, arthritis, and cutaneous manifestations who was ultimately diagnosed with Behçet's disease. The diagnosis was based on clinical evaluation and supported by the presence of HLA-B51, as well as the exclusion of other possible causes. Following a multidisciplinary approach involving infectious disease, rheumatology, and dermatology specialists, targeted immunosuppressive therapy was initiated, resulting in a very good clinical response. The case highlights the importance of considering Behçet's disease even in patients without travel history and underscores the value of interdisciplinary collaboration in timely diagnosis and treatment. Keywords: Behçet's disease, systemic vasculitis, ulceration, HLA-B51, fever of unknown origin.

items.title: Photo-activatable targeted hybrid extracellular vesicles for local inflammasome modulation in acute gouty arthritis.
items.abstract: Acute gouty arthritis is driven by monosodium urate (MSU)-induced NLRP3 inflammasome activation and IL-1β release, yet local and controllable immunomodulation remains challenging. Here, we developed pFusion@EV, a photo-activatable hybrid extracellular vesicle generated by fusing engineered 293 T-derived EVs with bone marrow mesenchymal stromal cell-derived EVs (BMSC@EV). The engineered EV membrane presents a TNFR1-binding peptide and a CD9-linked photosensitive IL-10 module, and a brief ex vivo 405-nm illumination step increases IL-10-associated bioactivity before administration. In THP-1 cells, IL-10 neutralization or deletion markedly reduced STAT3 phosphorylation, whereas TNFR1 blockade or deletion of the targeting peptide partially attenuated the response, supporting IL-10-dependent and targeting-enhanced signaling. pFusion@EV reduced macrophage oxidative stress, inflammasome-associated signaling, and pyroptosis-associated phenotypes and attenuated MSU-induced matrix-catabolic and autophagy-marker changes in chondrocytes. In acute murine air-pouch and ankle models, pFusion@EV increased local retention and reduced inflammatory-cell infiltration, IL-1β-associated responses, and early cartilage-matrix changes. These findings support ex vivo-activated pFusion@EV as a locally administered vesicular platform for modulating acute gouty arthritis but long-term structural joint protection remains to be established.

items.title: Evaluation of carotid artery stiffness by shear wave elastography in patients with rheumatoid arthritis.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is associated with increased cardiovascular risk and accelerated atherosclerosis secondary to chronic inflammation. Carotid intima-media thickness (IMT) is widely used for vascular assessment; however, arterial stiffness may reflect earlier vascular dysfunction. This study evaluated carotid artery stiffness using shear wave elastography (SWE) and investigated its complementary role alongside IMT in patients with RA. This cross-sectional study included patients with RA and healthy controls. Bilateral common carotid arteries were assessed using B-mode ultrasound and SWE. Carotid IMT, carotid stiffness, and carotid narrowing were evaluated. Clinical and inflammatory markers, including C-reactive protein (CRP) and erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), were analyzed. Combined carotid stiffness was significantly higher in patients with RA compared with controls (53.53 ± 12.28 vs. 48.46 ± 14.70, p = 0.034), while carotid IMT measurements did not significantly differ between groups. After multivariable adjustment, the association between RA and carotid stiffness became non-significant (p = 0.076). Carotid stiffness demonstrated significant positive correlations with CRP and ESR, whereas inflammatory markers were not associated with IMT. Patients with RA demonstrated increased carotid artery stiffness despite comparable IMT measurements. SWE may provide complementary value to conventional IMT assessment for detecting early vascular functional changes in RA.

items.title: Safety of TNF-α inhibitors, IL-17 inhibitors, and JAK inhibitors in the treatment of axial spondyloarthritis: a protocol for a multi-method study integrating FAERS data mining, dose-response network meta-analysis, and drug-target Mendelian randomization.
items.abstract: Biological and targeted synthetic disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs (b/tsDMARDs), including tumor necrosis factor-α inhibitors (TNFi), interleukin-17 inhibitors (IL-17i), and Janus kinase inhibitors (JAKi), are standard treatments for axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA). However, comparative evidence on the safety profiles of these three drug classes, particularly regarding infection-related adverse events, remains limited. No previous study has simultaneously integrated real-world pharmacovigilance data, interventional trial evidence, and causal inference methods within a triangulation framework to systematically evaluate the safety of these agents in axSpA. This study will employ three complementary components. First, a disproportionality analysis of the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) database (Q1 2004-Q4 2025) will use four signal detection algorithms (ROR, PRR, MGPS, BCPNN), supplemented by time-to-onset analysis (Weibull distribution), geographic analysis, and a weighted composite scoring system. Only drug-event combinations where the target drug is coded as Primary Suspect (PS) will be included in the primary analysis. Second, a systematic review incorporating dose-response network meta-analysis (NMA) of double-blind randomized controlled trials will focus on upper respiratory tract infections (URTIs) and opportunistic infections (OIs), with OIs analyzed by subtype (tuberculosis, herpes zoster, candidiasis, PJP). An Emax dose-response model will serve as the primary analytical approach, with linear and conventional NMA models as fallbacks. Databases will include PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library (CENTRAL), Web of Science, MEDLINE via Ovid, SCOPUS, and ProQuest, in addition to the ClinicalTrials.gov trial registry. The certainty of evidence will be assessed using the CINeMA framework. Third, multivariable Mendelian randomization (MVMR) and causal mediation analysis (FLOW-MR) will employ a sequential complementary framework: MVMR will estimate independent direct effects of each drug target pathway on infection outcomes while conditioning on AS, and FLOW-MR will decompose these effects along the temporal causal cascade (AS → drug target pathway → infection outcome), enabling mediation-based target validation. Signals identified for URTIs and OIs from both FAERS and NMA will be carried forward to the final triangulation stage. By triangulating evidence from real-world pharmacovigilance, randomized trials, and genetic causal inference within a structured qualitative framework with pre-specified convergence criteria, this multi-method protocol will provide a comprehensive and robust safety evaluation of b/tsDMARDs in axSpA. The integration of dose-response modeling and a sequential MVMR-to-FLOW-MR drug-target Mendelian randomization strategy represents a methodological advancement in the safety assessment of biologic therapies. Findings will inform clinical decision-making regarding the comparative safety of these agents. PROSPERO CRD420261417010.

items.title: Diffuse alveolar hemorrhage and myositis complicating eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis: a case report and narrative review.
items.abstract: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) is an uncommon antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)-associated vasculitis characterized by asthma, eosinophilia, and multisystem involvement. Diffuse alveolar hemorrhage and myositis are both infrequent manifestations of EGPA, and their co-occurrence in the same patient has rarely been reported. A 46-year-old man with adult-onset asthma, chronic sinusitis, and marked peripheral eosinophilia was diagnosed with EGPA in 2015. Over six years of follow-up, he had recurrent pulmonary relapses with migratory infiltrates and developed gastrointestinal involvement, nondilated cardiomyopathy, coronary artery disease, myositis, and diffuse alveolar hemorrhage; he was positive for myeloperoxidase (MPO)-ANCA. Disease activity persisted despite high-dose glucocorticoids, azathioprine, cyclophosphamide, and mycophenolate mofetil. Because the disease was severe, organ-threatening, and predominantly vasculitic, an anti-interleukin-5 agent was not chosen for remission induction; instead, rituximab was started and induced sustained remission. This case illustrates that refractory, MPO-ANCA-positive EGPA may respond to B-cell depletion with rituximab. The randomized REOVAS trial did not show rituximab to be superior to conventional remission-induction therapy; however, it was not designed to establish equivalence with cyclophosphamide in severe disease, and the optimal strategy for severe refractory disease remains undefined. ANCA status, together with the pattern and severity of organ involvement, may help individualize treatment in this setting.

items.title: Opportunistic abdominal aortic calcification assessment on spine radiographs in women with longstanding rheumatoid arthritis: linking cardiovascular burden and femoral neck bone loss.
items.abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) and osteoporosis are major comorbidities in rheumatoid arthritis (RA). We assessed abdominal aortic calcification (AAC) opportunistically on spine radiographs and examined its associations with CVD, estimated cardiovascular risk, bone mineral density (BMD), and fragility fractures in women with longstanding RA. This cross-sectional study included 196 consecutive women with longstanding RA followed at a tertiary hospital. All underwent dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry and conventional spine radiography. AAC was graded using the Kauppila score (KS) and categorized as absent, mild-to-moderate (KS 1-6), or extended (KS > 6). Multivariable models evaluated factors associated with AAC and overt CVD. Participants had a mean age of 62.8 ± 9.6 years and median RA duration of 21 years. AAC was present in 48 women (24.5%), including extended AAC in 25 (12.7%). Overt CVD was documented in 32 participants (16.3%). Extended AAC was independently associated with hypertension (OR 8.57, 95% CI 1.10-67.02), longer RA duration (OR 1.05 per year, 95% CI 1.004-1.09), and lower femoral neck T-score (OR 0.57, 95% CI 0.35-0.95). AAC of any severity was associated with overt CVD (OR 2.89, 95% CI 1.26-6.63). AAC detected on routine spine radiographs was common among women with longstanding RA and was associated with cardiovascular burden and lower femoral neck BMD. Opportunistic AAC assessment may complement cardiovascular and skeletal risk evaluation in RA. Larger cohorts are needed to confirm these exploratory associations, and prospective studies are needed to establish predictive value.

items.title: Gut microbiota-CRAMP axis controls salivary gland immune homeostasis in Sjögren's disease.
items.abstract: Sjögren's disease (SjD) is a systemic autoimmune disorder marked by lymphocytic infiltration of exocrine glands. To date, its pathogenesis remains incompletely understood. Cathelicidins are a widespread family of host-defense antimicrobial peptides, primarily recognized for their antimicrobial properties, and are now increasingly appreciated for their immunomodulatory functions. However, the role of cathelicidin in the immunopathogenesis of SjD remains unknown. In this study, we investigated the effects of cathelicidin-related antimicrobial peptide (CRAMP) on SjD and the underlying mechanisms. Salivary gland tissues from SjD patients and controls were collected. Two established mouse models of SjD, i.e., the non-obese diabetic (NOD) mice that spontaneously develop SjD-like disease features, and salivary gland protein-induced experimental SjD mice, were used for the studies. Our data showed that salivary gland acinar cells produce cathelicidin, and that production is impaired in both SjD patients and mice compared to the control group. Moreover, CRAMP plays a protective role in SjD, as exogenous CRAMP administration improved the SjD phenotype, whereas CRAMP knockdown exacerbated disease severity. By combining RNA sequencing with pharmacological inhibitors, we demonstrated that CRAMP acts through formyl peptide receptor 2 (FPR2) to inhibit the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway, thereby reducing the autoimmune response in the salivary glands. Furthermore, we identified gut microbiota and its metabolite, propionic acid, as critical regulators of CRAMP expression in salivary gland acinar cells. Treatment with propionic acid or transfer of gut microbiota from a non-autoimmune control strain to SjD mice increased CRAMP levels and alleviated disease severity, highlighting a pivotal gut-salivary gland axis in SjD pathogenesis. Overall, these findings underscore the pivotal role of CRAMP in protecting against SjD and pave the way for future microbiota-based therapies.

items.title: Pharmaceutical blockade of the neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn) ameliorates autoimmunity, inflammation, and fibrosis in the antitopoisomerase-I antibody-driven mouse model of systemic sclerosis.
items.abstract: Several autoantibodies promote inflammation and fibrosis in systemic sclerosis (SSc). Efgartigimod, engineered to block the neonatal fragment crystallisable (Fc) receptor (FcRn) and reduce immunoglobulin G (IgG) autoantibody levels, is approved for autoantibody-driven generalised myasthenia gravis and chronic inflammatory demyelinating neuropathy. FcRn blockade with murinised efgartigimod (mEfgartigimod) and an FcRn-blocking IgG1 Fc fragment was evaluated in the topoisomerase-I (TopoI)-induced mouse model of autoimmunity-driven fibrosis. Effects were assessed by immunoglobulin levels, biochemical and histological fibrosis readouts, Olink analyses, RNA sequencing (RNA-Seq), and imaging mass cytometry (IMC). Both prophylactic and therapeutic mEfgartigimod ameliorated dermal and pulmonary fibrosis in TopoI mice, comparably to nintedanib. Bulk RNA-Seq analysis demonstrated FcRn blockade with mEfgartigimod downregulated inflammatory, autoimmune, and fibrotic signalling pathways, with reduced expression of Ccl chemokines, tumour necrosis factor superfamily cytokines, and type I interferon signalling components. IMC showed reduced accumulation of myofibroblasts, classically activated macrophages, dendritic cells, and T cells upon FcRn blockade. Single‑nucleus RNA-Seq revealed altered fibroblast-macrophage crosstalk, with decreases in myofibroblasts, inflammatory and neutrophil-like macrophages, and T cells with cell-type-specific transcriptional effects associated with reversal of profibrotic/inflammatory transcriptional programs. Consistent with these cellular changes, the circulating levels of Il1β and several chemokines were downregulated upon treatment, whereas antifibrotic mediators, such as Fgf21 and soluble Pd-l2, were upregulated. These findings highlight that FcRn blockers such as efgartigimod may have potential to simultaneously target autoimmune, inflammatory, and fibrotic features of SSc and highlight the potential of autoantibody-reducing therapies as disease-modifying approaches in SSc. A randomised, controlled phase 2 trial with efgartigimod in SSc is currently ongoing.

items.title: Colchicine formulation switching and escalation to anti-IL-1 therapy in familial Mediterranean fever: A single-center real-world study.
items.abstract: To evaluate the usage of colchicine formulations and anti-IL-1 therapy, identify the clinical and genetic factors associated with treatment escalation, and detail the reasons for colchicine formulation switching in patients with familial Mediterranean fever (FMF). This retrospective cohort with a cross-sectional assessment enrolled 128 patients diagnosed with FMF based on the Tel Hashomer criteria. To detect of the efficacy and the causes of switching among colchicine formulations and anti-interleukin-1 (IL-1) therapeutic interventions, comprehensive clinical, laboratory, and genetic profiles were systematically re-evaluated for all participants. A total of 128 patients were analyzed, of whom 80 (62.5%) were female, with a mean age of 37.8±12.9 years. 84 (65.6%) patients were receiving coated colchicine, 33 (26%) were on compressed colchicine, and 11 were treated with anti-interleukin-1 (IL-1) agents when data was collected. A transition from coated to compressed colchicine was performed in 44 patients. The primary indications for this switch included inadequate clinical response in 25 (56.8%) patients, colchicine intolerance in 9 (20.4%), and physician preference in 10 (22.7%). Analysis of the allelic distribution revealed that the M694V mutation was present in 59.6% of all patients with FMF. However, in patients requiring anti-IL-1 agents-typically indicating a more severe or colchicine-resistant disease course-the prevalence of this mutation rose to 83.3%. Similarly, the rate of M694V homozygosity in the anti-IL-1 subgroup was nearly threefold higher than that of the general study group (50.0% vs. 18.3%, respectively). Optimizing colchicine delivery by transitioning to compressed formulations appears to provide a feasible intermediary step prior to initiating anti-IL-1 agents in FMF management. While Exon 10 mutations, particularly M694V, appear more frequent in patients requiring anti-IL-1 agents, prospective studies and cost-effectiveness analyses are warranted to confirm these findings.

items.title: The Clinical Spectrum and Diagnostic Challenge of Abdominal Pain in Takayasu Arteritis: A Case-Based Review.
items.abstract: Takayasu arteritis (TA) is a large-vessel vasculitis predominantly affecting the aorta and its primary branches. It is rare in children, and it poses significant diagnostic challenges, including high risks of misdiagnosis and treatment delay. We report the case of a 13-year-old female patient whose sole initial manifestation was abdominal pain. Over a short disease course of two weeks, aside from persistently and markedly elevated C-reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate, she had no other typical symptoms of vasculitis. Initially evaluated by gastroenterology, she underwent a complex diagnostic process that ultimately led to imaging confirmation. To gain a deeper insight into this clinical presentation, we conducted a narrative review of existing relevant case reports alongside our present case. A targeted search of the PubMed and Scopus databases was performed, followed by descriptive summarization and analysis of the clinical features of the included cases. Both the present case and the literature review indicate that the clinical manifestations of TA are highly heterogeneous, and TA can be particularly insidious as the cause of abdominal pain. Clinicians should remain vigilant for the possibility of TA and actively consider it in patients with unexplained abdominal pain and persistently abnormal inflammatory markers, even in the absence of typical vascular symptoms. This also underscores the value of non-specific inflammatory markers as screening tools and the importance of multidisciplinary collaboration in identifying such rare diseases.

items.title: Protein citrullination and lipid metabolic dysregulation in rheumatoid arthritis: a bidirectional pathogenic loop.
items.abstract: Protein citrullination, a post-translational modification catalyzed by peptidyl arginine deiminases, is a hallmark of rheumatoid arthritis. It generates neoepitopes that drive anti-citrullinated protein antibody responses and contributes to the breakdown of immune tolerance. In parallel, lipidomic studies have revealed extensive lipid metabolic disturbances in patients with rheumatoid arthritis, affecting fatty acid metabolism, glycerophospholipid and sphingolipid remodeling, and cholesterol handling. These two pathological features have traditionally been studied in isolation. Evidence from separate experimental systems suggests possible links, although reciprocal regulation has not been established directly in RA. Citrullinated proteins can undergo conformational and charge alterations that influence their interactions with surrounding biomolecules, potentially affecting pathways that regulate the lipid environment of immune and synovial resident cells. Conversely, lipid-associated inflammatory signals could influence peptidyl arginine deiminase expression or activity and, in turn, the citrullinated protein repertoire. This review examines the evidence linking protein citrullination and lipid dysregulation in rheumatoid arthritis and proposes a bidirectional pathogenic loop as an explanatory model whose individual components have different levels of experimental support. This framework identifies measurable endpoints for joint citrullination-lipid profiling and for experiments that perturb each process in both directions; clinical applications require prospective validation.

items.title: Multidomain efficacy and safety of IL-17A and IL-17A/F inhibitors versus adalimumab in biologic-naïve psoriatic arthritis: A systematic review and Meta-analysis of comparative trials.
items.abstract: Interleukin-17 A and interleukin-17 A/F inhibitors (collectively, IL-17i) and adalimumab (ADA) effectively treat psoriatic arthritis (PsA), but comparative multidomain evidence remains limited. We compared their efficacy and safety in biologic-naïve PsA. PubMed, Embase and Cochrane CENTRAL were searched through April 2026 for randomised controlled trials comparing IL-17i with ADA. Outcomes encompassed musculoskeletal and skin disease activity, patient-reported outcomes, physical function, composite disease activity and safety. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed. Four trials (n = 2198) were included. No significant differences were observed in principal musculoskeletal, patient-reported, functional or minimal disease activity outcomes. IL-17i favoured near-complete skin clearance (PASI90, week 24: RR 1.38; 95% CI 1.19-1.61; p = 0.006; I 2  = 0%; k = 4) and combined joint-skin responses (ACR50/PASI100, week 52: RR 1.49; 95% CI 1.18-1.89; p = 0.02; I 2  = 0%; k = 3). Enthesitis resolution also favoured IL-17i at week 52 (RR 1.10; 95% CI 1.01-1.20; p = 0.04; I 2  = 0%; k = 3). At week 24, Candida infections were numerically higher with IL-17i in the primary analysis (OR 4.44; 95% CI 0.89-22.25; p = 0.06; I 2  = 0%; k = 3), with a significant Peto sensitivity estimate (OR 3.66; 95% CI 1.61-8.32; p = 0.002; I 2  = 0%; k = 3). IL-17i were also associated with fewer adverse-event discontinuations than ADA (OR 0.57; 95% CI 0.34-0.96; p = 0.04; I 2  = 0%; k = 3). IL-17i and ADA showed no significant differences in principal joint outcomes, while IL-17i favoured skin and combined joint-skin responses. Treatment selection should therefore be individualised according to the predominant disease domains and safety considerations, rather than assuming overall superiority of either treatment approach.

items.title: Epigenetic remodelling of DNA methylation shapes synovial macrophage-fibroblast-like synoviocytes crosstalk in rheumatoid arthritis.
items.abstract: Macrophages and fibroblast-like synoviocytes (FLSs) are key cellular components of the rheumatoid arthritis (RA) synovial microenvironment and together constitute a pathogenic niche that drives immune infiltration, synovial hyperplasia and joint destruction. Under physiological conditions, macrophages contribute to the maintenance of synovial immune balance and stromal homeostasis. Dysregulated macrophage-FLSs crosstalk amplifies inflammatory signalling, promotes invasive phenotypes and sustains chronic synovitis through self-reinforcing feedback mechanisms in RA. These processes are closely linked to epigenetic remodelling, which may precede clinical manifestations of disease. In RA, aberrant DNA methylation patterns reprogramme disease-relevant gene expression networks, involving DNMT-mediated methylation, TET-mediated active demethylation, UHRF1 maintenance, thereby influencing disease susceptibility, inflammation persistence, tissue invasiveness and therapeutic response. Moreover, DNA methylation acts in concert with other regulatory layers, including RNA methylation modification and histone modification, to shape the temporal and spatial heterogeneity of macrophage-FLSs crosstalk. Therefore, it is necessary to seek new therapeutic approaches. Targeting DNA methylation to regulate the inflammatory response and invasive function in cancer has shown clinical efficacy and provides a possibility for specifically targeting synovial macrophage-FLSs crosstalk. Therefore, targeted treatment of DNA methylation-driven crosstalk between macrophages and FLSs may be a promising alternative method for the prevention and treatment of RA.

items.title: What precedes the onset of systemic lupus erythematosus? From susceptibility to prediction and prevention.
items.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a complex autoimmune disease characterized by substantial clinical heterogeneity and delayed diagnosis. Increasing evidence from longitudinal studies indicates that immune dysregulation and autoreactive responses precede clinical manifestations by years, suggesting that SLE evolves through a prolonged preclinical continuum rather than an abrupt disease onset. During this period, genetic susceptibility, epigenetic alterations, and environmental exposures interact to progressively disrupt immune tolerance and promote autoimmunity. This review summarizes current advances in understanding the preclinical phases preceding SLE classification, focusing on the integrated susceptibility landscape and early immune alterations that drive disease progression. We discuss evolving concepts and definitions of preclinical and transitional states, including individuals with autoantibody positivity or autoimmune features who exhibit variable risks of progression. We further highlight emerging evidence of early immune perturbations, including interferon pathway activation, B- and T-cell dysregulation, and inflammatory responses, as well as their potential utility for predicting disease evolution. Finally, we discuss strategies for risk stratification and early intervention, emphasizing the potential of the preclinical window to enable personalized approaches for preventing or delaying SLE onset.

items.title: Catalpol alleviates glandular and pulmonary injury in primary Sjögren's syndrome via regulation of sphingolipid metabolism.
items.abstract: In traditional Chinese medicine, pSS-related oral and ocular dryness is associated with depletion of yin and body fluids, while pulmonary involvement may reflect impaired lung moistening. Rehmannia glutinosa is traditionally used to nourish yin, generate fluids, and relieve dryness. Catalpol, its major iridoid glycoside, may provide a pharmacological basis for these traditional uses. This study investigated the protective effects of catalpol in experimental pSS and examined the involvement of KDSR-mediated sphingolipid metabolism. An antigen-induced experimental Sjögren's syndrome (ESS) mouse model, interferon-γ-stimulated A253 cells, and transforming growth factor-β-stimulated NIH-3T3 fibroblasts were used. Pseudo-targeted sphingolipidomics, multi-cohort transcriptomic analysis, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, cellular thermal shift assays, and KDSR knockdown were performed. Catalpol improved salivary secretion and reduced glandular inflammation and epithelial apoptosis in ESS mice. It also attenuated ESS-associated pulmonary inflammation and fibrosis-related changes and suppressed fibroblast activation. Integrated sphingolipidomic and transcriptomic analyses identified disease-associated KDSR upregulation and alterations in the sphinganine/3-ketodihydrosphingosine ratio. Molecular simulation and cellular thermal shift assays supported a potential interaction between catalpol and KDSR. Catalpol reduced KDSR expression and inhibited integrin/FAK/MYH9 signaling, whereas KDSR knockdown attenuated its protective effects in vitro. Catalpol ameliorated glandular dysfunction and pulmonary injury in experimental pSS. These effects were associated with KDSR-mediated sphingolipid metabolism and suppression of integrin/FAK/MYH9 signaling.

items.title: Illness perceptions among adults aged 18-44 years with ankylosing spondylitis: A qualitative study informed by the common-sense model of self-regulation.
items.abstract: Ankylosing spondylitis mainly affects people in early and middle adulthood. This period involves important transitions in education, career, relationships, and family. Illness perceptions play an important role in treatment adherence and disease management. Few qualitative studies have examined how Chinese adults perceive and cope with the disease using a clear theoretical framework. This study aimed to explore illness perceptions among adults aged 18-44 years with ankylosing spondylitis, informed by the Common-Sense Model of Self-Regulation. This was a qualitative descriptive study conducted in a tertiary hospital in Nanjing, China. Sixteen adults aged 18-44 years with ankylosing spondylitis were recruited through maximum variation purposive sampling. Data were collected through face-to-face semi-structured interviews and analyzed using thematic analysis. Three themes were identified: fragmentation and biases in illness perceptions; disrupted daily life and recurring emotional burden; and negotiating control between professional support and experiential self-management. Illness perceptions among adults aged 18-44 years with ankylosing spondylitis were dynamic and context-dependent, influenced by symptom experiences, causal interpretations, perceived consequences, and ongoing negotiation between professional guidance and experiential self-management. Illness coherence did not necessarily increase with longer disease duration, and no consistent age-related pattern emerged. These findings offer insight into how adults with AS construct and adapt their illness perceptions, which may guide future patient-centered support.

items.title: Prevalence and prognostic significance of extrarenal manifestations in patients with lupus nephritis: A retrospective cohort study.
items.abstract: To evaluate the prevalence and prognostic implications of extrarenal involvement in lupus nephritis (LN), with emphasis on treatment response and the risk of future renal and extrarenal flares. We retrospectively reviewed patients newly diagnosed with LN between January 2006 and December 2022 and categorized them according to the presence of extrarenal involvement at diagnosis. Renal response and remission at 12 months, defined according to the Definition of Remission in SLE (DORIS), as well as the incidence of renal and extrarenal flares during follow-up, were compared between groups. Factors associated with DORIS remission and renal response were assessed using multivariable logistic regression analyses. Among 348 patients with LN, 156 (44.8%) had extrarenal involvement at diagnosis, most commonly hematological manifestations (59.0%). Rates of complete renal response (CRR) and DORIS remission at 12 months were comparable between patients with and without extrarenal involvement (CRR: 57.1% vs. 46.9%, p = 0.06; DORIS remission: 21.8% vs. 29.7%, p = 0.09). Over a median follow-up of 79.6 months, the incidence of renal flares (28.8% vs. 26.0%, p = 0.56) and extrarenal flares (26.3% vs. 24.5%, p = 0.74) did not differ significantly between groups. In multivariable analyses, baseline extrarenal involvement was not associated with DORIS remission (odds ratio [OR], 1.307; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.779-2.193; p = 0.310) or renal response (OR, 0.974; 95% CI: 0.564-1.682; p = 0.925). Extrarenal involvement is present in nearly half of patients at LN diagnosis, however, it does not appear to influence renal response, DORIS remission, or the long-term risk of renal or extrarenal flares.

items.title: Two-Year Treatment Persistence and Effectiveness of Ixekizumab in Psoriatic Arthritis in Italian Clinical Practice: Results from the ROUTE-IXE Study.
items.abstract: Randomised controlled trials have demonstrated the efficacy and safety of ixekizumab as a treatment for active psoriatic arthritis (PsA), and real-world evidence on long-term persistence and effectiveness is emerging. This study aimed to characterise ixekizumab use in the Italian routine clinical setting and provide insights into its persistence and effectiveness, complementing real-world evidence from single-country cohorts and multinational studies. This descriptive, multicentre, retrospective study was conducted in Italy in adult patients with PsA who received a first prescription of ixekizumab after January 2021 and had a minimum of three subsequent evaluations. The primary objective was to describe treatment persistence at week 104. Secondary objectives aimed to describe patients' demographic and clinical characteristics and evaluate treatment persistence and effectiveness at weeks 12, 24, 52 and 104. A total of 204 patients, of whom 88 (43.1%) were male and 116 (56.9%) were female, were eligible for inclusion in the study. The mean (standard deviation) age was 55.8 (11.0) years. Comorbidities were present in 66.7% (n = 136) of patients, with the majority being cardiometabolic disorders. The median (interquartile range) disease duration was 5.3 (2.4-12.2) years. Peripheral joint involvement was the most common PsA manifestation (66.7%, n = 136), followed by mixed symptoms (28.4%, n = 58) and axial-only symptoms (4.9%, n = 10). Most patients (74.5%, n = 152) had prior exposure to biologic therapy; most also presented with high or moderate disease activity (84.6%, n = 132). Treatment persistence at week 104 was 78.6% (n = 158), and the Kaplan-Meier estimate was 0.800 (95% confidence interval 0.736-0.850). Disease activity progressively improved. At week 104, 45.3% (n = 72) of patients had low disease activity, and 25.2% (n = 40) were in remission; 34.1% (n = 31) achieved very low disease activity, and, among patients with axial involvement, 61.9% (n = 26) had inactive or mild disease. Ixekizumab showed high 2-year treatment persistence and effectiveness in the treatment of patients with PsA and complex disease profiles, supporting its value in informing treatment decisions and optimising patient outcomes.

items.title: Dietary index for gut microbiota and self-reported rheumatoid arthritis among U.S. adults: a cross-sectional study.
items.abstract: To investigate the association between dietary index for gut microbiota (DI-GM) scores and self-reported rheumatoid arthritis (RA), assessing microbiota-related dietary patterns in a cross-sectional population. Cross-sectional analysis of NHANES data from 2007 to 2018, including 3057 participants (792 with self-reported RA). Two 24-h dietary recalls were used to calculate DI-GM scores. Weighted multivariate logistic regression, restricted cubic spline functions, exploratory subgroup analyses, and weighted quantile sum regression were performed to assess DI-GM-RA associations. RA participants had significantly lower DI-GM scores than controls (4.55 ± 1.67 vs. 4.86 ± 1.66, p < 0.001). Higher DI-GM scores were associated with lower odds of self-reported RA: fully adjusted OR 0.91 (95% CI 0.84-1.00, p = 0.047) for continuous scores and 0.49 (95% CI 0.24-1.00, p = 0.049) for the highest category. Educational attainment was the only subgroup characteristic showing a significant interaction (p for interaction = 0.031). Weighted quantile sum analysis identified chickpeas (33.0%), avocados (23.4%), dietary fiber (9.5%), and coffee (8.1%) as the main contributors to the observed dietary association. Higher DI-GM scores were modestly associated with lower odds of self-reported RA. Given the cross-sectional design and potential for outcome misclassification and reverse causation, these findings should be interpreted cautiously and require confirmation in prospective studies. Key Points • Higher dietary index for gut microbiota (DI-GM) scores were associated with lower odds of self-reported rheumatoid arthritis among U.S. adults. • Educational attainment was the only subgroup characteristic showing a statistically significant interaction; subgroup findings should be considered exploratory. • Chickpeas, avocados, dietary fiber, and coffee accounted for 74.0% of the total weighted quantile sum weight. • The cross-sectional design, self-reported outcome, and potential reverse causation limit causal interpretation.

items.title: Ruxolitinib improves outcomes in association with altered fibroblast immunobiology in mouse models of Sjögren's disease.
items.abstract: Sjögren Disease (SjD) is a common rheumatologic disease with symptoms of dryness attributed to autoimmune exocrinopathy. JAK-STAT signaling pathway activity contributes to SjD salivary gland pathogenesis. We hypothesized that treatment of SjD model mice with ruxolitinib, a JAK-inhibitor, would improve disease course. NOD.B10 and Aec SjD model mice were treated with vehicle or ruxolitinib for two weeks. We measured plasma immunoglobulins and cytokines, and assessed submandibular salivary glands (SMSGs) histologically, with flow cytometry, and spatial transcriptomics. Aec mice had a more robust inflammatory profile than NOD.B10 mice as measured by SMSG lymphocytic infiltrate, peripheral immunoglobulins and cytokine concentrations. Ruxolitinib treatment reduced plasma [IgG], [CXCL13], and focus score in Aec but not NOD.B10 mice. In Aec mice, flow cytometry showed reductions in phosphorylated (p) STAT1 in SMSG epithelial cells, leukocytes, and fibroblasts with treatment. pSTAT1 correlated with salivary flow rate and focus score. Spatial transcriptomic sequencing and immunofluorescence of SMSGs revealed a treatment effect upon fibroblast-macrophage spatial relationships. Ruxolitinib treatment improved disease course in Aec mice but not NOD.B10 mice, suggesting these mice model different SjD subpopulations and ruxolitinib efficacy may be subpopulation dependent. Flow cytometry, spatial transcriptomics, and immunostaining results implicated ruxolitinib-induced changes of fibroblast-immune cell interactions in the SMSG thereby suggesting these unique interactions as a pathogenic element and novel treatment target. These results underscore the therapeutic potential of JAK-STAT pathway inhibition for treatment of SjD, and with ruxolitinib specifically, at least for specific SjD subpopulations.

items.title: Comparative Efficacy of Different Biologic Agents on Radiographic Progression in Patients with Rheumatoid Arthritis: A Network Meta-Analysis.
items.abstract: Radiographic progression in rheumatoid arthritis (RA) reflects irreversible joint damage. Whether different classes of biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (bDMARDs) offer comparable structural protection remains uncertain. To compare six bDMARD classes (tumor necrosis factor [TNF]-α inhibitors, interleukin [IL]-17 inhibitors, T-cell co-stimulation modulators, B-cell depleting agents, IL-6 receptor antagonists, and IL-23 inhibitors) in suppressing radiographic progression in RA. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and CENTRAL were searched to 31 December 2025 for randomized controlled trials (RCT); change in modified Total Sharp Score (mTSS) at 12 months was the primary outcome. A Bayesian random-effects network meta-analysis was fitted, with SUCRA-based ranking. 27 RCTs (11,650 patients) were included. All six classes significantly inhibited mTSS progression versus placebo. Relative to TNF-α inhibitors (TNF-i), greater inhibition was seen with B-cell depleting agents (mean difference [MD] = -18.46, 95% CI -20.86 to -16.06), IL-23 inhibitors (MD = -18.14, 95% CI -21.11 to -15.16), IL-17 inhibitors (MD = -15.67), T-cell co-stimulation modulators (MD = -14.99) and IL-6 receptor antagonists (MD = -13.73); the first two were also superior to IL-6 receptor antagonists. For bone erosion (13 RCTs), IL-17, B-cell depleting, IL-6 receptor and T-cell agents, but not IL-23 inhibitors, were superior to TNF-i. For ACR20 (20 RCTs), IL-23 (OR = 2.75, 95% CI 1.31-5.76), IL-6 (OR = 2.12) and IL-17 (OR = 1.86) inhibitors were superior to TNF-i. Serious adverse events (10 RCTs) did not differ from placebo. B-cell depleting agents and IL-23 inhibitors ranked highest; as several comparisons rest on few trials, this ordering is hypothesis generating.

items.title: Risk Factors for Gout Flares After Urate-Lowering Therapy: A Nationwide Prospective Cohort Study.
items.abstract: Gout is an inflammatory arthritis caused by the monosodium urate crystal deposition in joints, with some patients experiencing recurrent flares. This study compared the clinical characteristics of patients who experienced gout flares with those who did not. Data were analyzed from the Urate Lowering TheRApy in Gout registry, including adults aged ≥ 18 years who met the 2015 American College of Rheumatology/European League Against Rheumatism gout classification criteria. Patients were designated into flare or no-flare groups based on the occurrence of at least one gout flare within the first 6 months. Among 327 patients, 29.0% experienced at least one gout flare within 6 months. Compared with the no-flare group, patients with flares had higher gout impact scale ( P = 0.019) and EuroQoL 5-Dimension 3-Level scores ( P = 0.012), and more frequent bone erosion ( P < 0.001), and tophi ( P = 0.031). Multivariate logistic regression showed that radiographic bone erosion ( P = 0.013) and poorer quality of life (gout impact scale, P = 0.037; EuroQoL 5-Dimension 3-Level scores, P = 0.014) were independently associated with increased gout flare risk. Fewer patients in the flare group achieved target serum urate levels at 6 months ( P = 0.006). Impaired quality of life, and radiographic evidence of bone erosion were identified as independent risk factors for gout flare in this prospective cohort study. These findings highlight the importance of comprehensive clinical assessment to identify high-risk patients for future flares and optimize individualized management strategies.
