items.title: Severe Organ Involvement in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus: A Retrospective Single-Center Study From Morocco.
items.abstract: Introduction Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a chronic autoimmune disease characterized by multisystem inflammatory involvement and an unpredictable clinical course. SLE is among the most prevalent autoimmune diseases in Morocco, yet epidemiological and clinical data from this region remain limited. Disease management relies mainly on conventional therapies, with restricted access to advanced targeted treatments. Objective To describe the epidemiological, clinical, biological, and therapeutic characteristics of patients diagnosed with SLE in an internal medicine department in Morocco, with a particular focus on severe renal, hematological, and neurological manifestations. Methods We conducted a retrospective descriptive study including 61 patients diagnosed with SLE between January 2017 and September 2022 at the Internal Medicine Department of the International University Hospital Cheikh Khalifa Ibn Zaid in Casablanca, Morocco. Diagnosis was established according to the 2019 European League Against Rheumatism/American College of Rheumatology (EULAR/ACR) and/or the 2012 Systemic Lupus International Collaborating Clinics (SLICC) classification criteria. Data were collected from medical records and analyzed using descriptive statistical methods. Results The study population was predominantly female (n=55; 90.2%), with a mean age at diagnosis of 40.3 years (SD 14.2; median 40; range 13-74). The most common manifestations were fatigue (82.0%), arthralgia (70.5%), and malar rash (59.0%). Hematological involvement was prominent: anemia was present in 29 patients (47.5%), of whom 10 (16.4%) had confirmed autoimmune hemolytic anemia (AIHA). Renal involvement was identified in 10 patients (16.4%); among the seven who underwent biopsy, class IV lupus nephritis predominated (n=5; 71.4%). Neurological involvement was documented in 14 patients (22.5%), with the majority comprising nonfocal manifestations such as persistent headaches and mood disorders. Most patients were treated with hydroxychloroquine (n=48; 78.7%) and systemic corticosteroids (n=38; 62.3%); immunomodulatory therapy was required in 18 patients (29.5%). Of the 39 patients with complete follow-up (median 28 months), 14 (35.9%) achieved complete remission, 19 (48.7%) achieved partial remission, 13 (33.3%) experienced disease relapse, and six (15.4%) achieved neither. Conclusion This single-center Moroccan cohort highlights a substantial burden of hematological involvement and reveals a treatment landscape defined by restricted access to biologic therapies. The findings underscore the need for region-specific epidemiological data, improved access to targeted treatments, and dedicated prospective research to better characterize SLE in North African populations.

items.title: MIS-C Followed by Systemic Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis: A Diagnostic Challenge in a Child.
items.abstract: Multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C) is a severe postinfectious inflammatory condition associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection and characterized by immune dysregulation with hyperinflammation and multisystem involvement. Its clinical manifestations may overlap with other pediatric inflammatory disorders, including systemic-onset juvenile idiopathic arthritis (sJIA), creating diagnostic challenges. We report the case of a 9-year-old child who presented with a 7-day history of high fever, fatigue, myalgia, arthralgia, anorexia, gastrointestinal symptoms, and a transient maculopapular rash. Laboratory investigations revealed marked systemic inflammation, including leukocytosis, neutrophilia, elevated C-reactive protein, ferritin, and fibrinogen levels. The patient also had gastrointestinal, mucocutaneous, and respiratory involvement, with positive anti-SARS-CoV-2 IgG antibodies. Based on the clinical and laboratory findings, MIS-C was diagnosed and treated with intravenous immunoglobulin and systemic corticosteroids, resulting in complete clinical recovery and normalization of inflammatory markers. Approximately 2 weeks after discharge, the child was readmitted with recurrent high fever, fatigue, myalgia, arthralgia, and anorexia. Inflammatory markers were again markedly elevated, with a substantial increase in ferritin levels. Musculoskeletal ultrasonography demonstrated synovial inflammation and joint effusion involving the knee and sacroiliac joints. In light of the emergence of objective synovitis and persistent systemic inflammation, the diagnosis was revised to sJIA. Treatment with nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, systemic glucocorticoids, and methotrexate resulted in clinical improvement and subsequent remission. The recurrence of fever and systemic inflammation after apparent clinical and laboratory resolution of MIS-C should prompt careful reassessment of the diagnosis and consideration of other inflammatory disorders. The subsequent emergence of objective arthritis or synovitis may be an important clue to underlying sJIA.

items.title: Pyruvate Kinase M2-Mediated H3K9 Lactylation and XBP1 Signaling Positive Feedback Loop Facilitates CD4 + T Cell Spinal Recruitment and Central Sensitization in Rheumatoid Arthritis.
items.abstract: Central sensitization is a critical pathophysiological mechanism underlying chronic pain in rheumatoid arthritis (RA). CD4 + T cells not only promote chronic inflammation in RA but may also migrate into the central nervous system to stimulate central sensitization. However, the regulatory mechanism by which CD4 + T cells contribute to central sensitization in RA remains unclear. In this study, we report that CD4 + T cells were significantly accumulated in the spinal dorsal horn (SDH) of collagen-induced arthritis (CIA) mice and promoted their central sensitization-like behaviors. Mechanistically, PKM2-dependent lactate facilitated H3K9 lactylation (H3K9la) in CD4 + T cells. H3K9la was highly enriched at the promoters of XBP1, which facilitated the transcription of KIF4 and MYO1B and the accumulation of CD4 + T cells in SDH. Furthermore, XBP1 may facilitate the transcription of PKM2, establishing a positive feedback loop between PKM2-induced H3K9la and XBP1 signaling in CIA mice. Crucially, the clinical relevance of this pathway was validated in patients with RA, where the expression of PKM2/H3K9la/XBP1 was significantly increased and positively correlated with central sensitization scores. Overall, our study indicates a positive feedback loop of PKM2/H3K9la/XBP1 in facilitating CD4 + T cell spinal recruitment, which may provide a promising therapeutic strategy for mitigating central sensitization in RA.

items.title: Anti-phosphatidylserine/prothrombin antibodies in antiphospholipid syndrome: Clinical associations and methodological heterogeneity-a scoping review.
items.abstract: To map the clinical and laboratory evidence for anti-phosphatidylserine/prothrombin (aPS/PT) antibodies in antiphospholipid syndrome (APS), identify the settings in which testing may add value beyond conventional antiphospholipid antibodies (aPL), and define the methodological barriers to wider clinical implementation. We conducted a prospectively registered scoping review in accordance with PRISMA-ScR. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched for human studies published from January 2000 onward that evaluated aPS/PT antibodies in APS or seronegative APS (SN-APS). Clinical associations, laboratory correlations, assay characteristics, cut-off definitions, titre reporting, and persistence were synthesized descriptively. Fifty-eight studies were included. Associations with thrombosis were evaluated in 36 studies, of which 32 reported a positive relationship. Pregnancy morbidity was assessed in 36 studies, with 21 reporting a positive association, although outcome definitions were highly variable. The most consistent laboratory finding was the association between aPS/PT and lupus anticoagulant (LA): 31 of 35 studies reported a positive relationship. Twenty-two studies included patients with SN-APS, but only six specifically examined aPS/PT in this population. Commercial assays were used in 42 studies, predominantly ELISA, yet cut-off selection, titre reporting, and confirmation of persistence varied substantially. Only 11 studies assessed persistence at least 12 weeks apart. aPS/PT antibodies show a reproducible clinical and laboratory signal across the APS spectrum, but their immediate value is most likely as a selective adjunct in diagnostically challenging settings rather than as a universal fourth criterion antibody. Prospective multicentre studies using harmonized assays must establish whether aPS/PT provides independent diagnostic or prognostic information beyond LA and conventional aPL profiles.

items.title: MARCH5 Links Hypoxia to Neutrophil Ferroptosis in SLE via FSP1 Ubiquitination.
items.abstract: Ferroptosis plays an important role in the progression of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). This study aims to investigate the molecular mechanism by which membrane-associated RING-CH-type finger protein 5 (MARCH5) regulates ferroptosis suppressor protein 1 (FSP1), a key regulator of ferroptosis resistance, under hypoxic conditions and its impact on SLE progression. We established a Toll-like receptor 7/8 (TLR7/8) agonist-induced mouse model of SLE under normoxic or hypoxic conditions and longitudinally evaluated pathological manifestations and survival. In vitro, the effects of hypoxia on ferroptosis induced by glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) inhibitors or FSP1 inhibitors were assessed using the Cell Counting Kit-8 (CCK-8) assay. Cycloheximide (CHX) chase assays and pharmacological inhibitors of protein degradation pathways were employed to investigate how hypoxia regulates FSP1 stability. Candidate E3 ligases involved in FSP1 ubiquitination were identified using bioinformatic prediction tools and validated through March5 knockdown or overexpression experiments. Finally, neutrophil-specific March5 knockout mice were generated to further demonstrate that hypoxia promotes SLE progression through a MARCH5-dependent mechanism. Chronic hypoxia significantly exacerbates SLE pathology by selectively disrupting FSP1-dependent, rather than GPX4-dependent, ferroptosis resistance in neutrophils. Mechanistically, hypoxia does not affect Aifm2 (i.e., the gene encoding FSP1) mRNA expression but accelerates FSP1 protein degradation through MARCH5-mediated ubiquitination and proteasomal turnover. Hypoxia enhances the interaction between MARCH5 and FSP1, promoting FSP1 destabilization. Knockdown of MARCH5 prevents hypoxia-induced FSP1 degradation and neutrophil ferroptosis, whereas neutrophil-specific March5 deletion improves survival, reduces autoantibody production, restores complement levels, and alleviates organ damage in SLE mice. This study reveals a pathogenic axis whereby hypoxia compromises neutrophil ferroptosis resistance and exacerbates SLE progression through MARCH5-mediated ubiquitination and degradation of FSP1. These findings elucidate how impaired FSP1-dependent ferroptosis defense contributes to chronic inflammatory disease progression and identify the MARCH5-FSP1 interaction as a potential therapeutic target for SLE and other ferroptosis-associated autoimmune disorders.

items.title: Performance Status as a Prognostic Factor in Japanese Patients With Myeloperoxidase-Antineutrophil Cytoplasmic Antibody-Positive Microscopic Polyangiitis.
items.abstract: This observational study investigated the impact of performance status (PS) on prognosis following remission induction therapy in patients with myeloperoxidase (MPO)-antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody-positive microscopic polyangiitis (MPA). Patients with MPO-antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody-positive MPA (MPO-MPA) and serum creatinine <5.0 mg/dL who were treated at Iwate Prefectural Central Hospital or enrolled in a Japanese multicenter prospective database were included. Patients were categorized by PS (good [0-1] vs poor [2-4]). Remission induction therapy was categorized as glucocorticoid (GC) monotherapy or combination therapy (GC plus immunosuppressants). The primary endpoint was a composite of death or end-stage kidney disease (ESKD). Outcomes were compared between the PS groups using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox proportional hazards models, with stratification by induction therapy. Of 290 patients, 189 had good PS. Combination therapy was administered in 28% of patients (cyclophosphamide, 92%; rituximab, 8%). The poor PS group featured an older patient age and higher Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score (BVAS). In the cohort-stratified multivariable Cox model adjusted for age, sex, and BVAS, poor PS was independently associated with a higher risk of death or ESKD (hazard ratio [HR] 2.23, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.09-4.55). Other risk factors included older age and male sex. In exploratory, hypothesis-generating stratified analyses, the adjusted HRs for poor PS were 1.35 (95% CI 0.57-3.21) and 4.52 (95% CI 1.25-16.30) in the GC monotherapy and combination therapy groups, respectively. Poor PS was independently associated with an increased risk of death or ESKD in patients with MPO-MPA.

items.title: Factors Associated With Early Axial Spondyloarthritis in a Multiethnic Asian Cohort in Singapore.
items.abstract: Early diagnosis is crucial in disease management and improving patient outcomes in axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA). Patients with early axSpA may have distinct clinical profiles. We aim to evaluate factors associated with early axSpA in a multiethnic Asian cohort in Singapore. A cross-sectional analysis of a prospective cohort was performed. Patients diagnosed with axSpA by a rheumatologist and fulfilling the 2009 ASAS classification criteria for axSpA were included. Patients were classified as early axSpA if the duration of their axial symptoms was 2 years or shorter. We compared disease characteristics, comorbidities, and patient-reported outcomes for early and non-early axSpA patients. Univariable analyses were conducted, and factors with p < 0.1 were included in the multivariable logistic regressions to identify factors associated with early axSpA. A total of 360 patients were included, 83 (23%) female and 322 (89%) Chinese. Only 49 (14%) were classified as early axSpA. Patients with early axSpA were younger [mean (SD) age: 34.7 (11.6) vs. 41.9 (13.5) years, p < 0.01], has a higher proportion of female patients (41% vs. 20%, p < 0.01), and were less likely to be HLA-B27 positive (74% vs. 86%, p = 0.03), and having radiographic sacroiliitis (52% vs. 83%, p < 0.01). Patients with early axSpA had higher disease activity [mean ASDAS (S.D.): 2.6 (1.2) vs. 2.1 (0.9), p = 0.02] and reported worse health and functioning [mean ASAS HI (S.D.): 6.1 (3.8) vs. 4.8 (3.7), p = 0.03]. About 1 in every 7 patients with axSpA presented early in the course of their disease. Patients with early axSpA were more likely females, younger, less likely to have radiographic sacroiliitis, but had higher disease activity.

items.title: Regulatory T cell dysfunction and therapeutic advances in rheumatoid arthritis, psoriasis, vitiligo, and systemic lupus erythematosus.
items.abstract: Regulatory T cells (Tregs) are a critical immunosuppressive subset of CD4+ T cells, whose lineage stability and suppressive function rely on the transcription factor FOXP3 . Within inflamed tissue microenvironments, Tregs maintain immune homeostasis and preserve tissue integrity via multiple mechanisms, including secretion of anti-inflammatory cytokines such as IL-10 and TGF-β, CD39/CD73-mediated adenosine metabolic pathways, and CTLA-4-dependent cell-contact inhibition. Nevertheless, in autoimmune diseases including systemic lupus erythematosus, psoriasis, rheumatoid arthritis, and vitiligo, Tregs frequently exhibit reduced frequency, impaired suppressive capacity, and conversion to pro-inflammatory phenotypes, accompanied by excessive activation of Th17 cells. This results in severe disruption of the Th17/Treg immune axis, which drives chronic inflammation and tissue damage. In terms of therapeutic strategies, low-dose IL-2 selectively expands functional Tregs to restore systemic immune balance. Rapamycin reverses Treg depletion and dysfunction by inhibiting the mTOR pathway, thereby reconstructing an immune-tolerant tissue microenvironment. Furthermore, engineered CAR-Treg cells exert antigen-specific anti-inflammatory effects, offering a novel therapeutic option for autoimmune diseases. Although these interventions have demonstrated promising efficacy in preclinical and early clinical studies, their clinical translation is hindered by major bottlenecks, such as precise targeting of inflamed tissues, sustained stability of Treg function under inflammatory conditions, and avoidance of systemic immunosuppressive risks. This paper systematically reviews the regulatory mechanisms and targeted therapeutic advances of Tregs in autoimmune diseases linked to Th17/Treg imbalance, analyzes the limitations of current research, and provides theoretical evidence for precision immunotherapy of autoimmune diseases.

items.title: Can nutrition prevent the onset of Rheumatoid Arthritis? A mini review of dietary risk and progression from pre-clinical autoimmunity.
items.abstract: Rheumatic and musculoskeletal diseases are major causes of disability worldwide, and many have inflammation at their core. Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA), in particular, is preceded by a prolonged "pre-clinical" phase in which genetic susceptibility and modifiable exposures, including diet, interact. Nutrition is thought to play an important role as an 'external' but modifiable factor in inflammatory diseases. The existing literature suggests that it may act as a lever for prevention and risk modification through direct or indirect effects on adiposity, systemic inflammation, mucosal immunity, the gut microbiome, and cardiometabolic comorbidity. In this mini review, we synthesize and critically appraise the evidence linking dietary patterns and targeted nutritional interventions with RA risk.

items.title: MHC-II + G-MDSC expressing CD80, CD86, or ICOSL are associated with pro-inflammatory CD4 + T cells phenotypes in the lungs of lupus-prone mice.
items.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a chronic inflammatory autoimmune disease that affects various tissues of the body. One of these tissues is the lung, in which pleuropulmonary manifestations commonly occur. In these patients, homeostasis is disrupted, characterized by a decrease in T reg and an increase in T h1 and T h2 cells. Myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs) are a cell population characterized by their ability to suppress the T cell response; however, in recent years, the presence of major histocompatibility complex class II (MHC-II) molecules on MDSCs has been reported. Nevertheless, the presence of costimulatory molecules, such as CD80, CD86, and ICOSL, has not been studied yet in MDSCs expressing MHC-II in the context of SLE. In this study, we evaluated the pulmonary microenvironment in SLE mice from an immunological and histological perspective. We observed increased pro-inflammatory cytokines and cellular infiltration in lungs of SLE mice. We also observed MDSC MHC-II cells expressing CD80, CD86, and ICOSL in this tissue, along with alterations of CD4 + T cells subsets, characterized by a decrease in IL-10 frequency in SLE mice. Moreover, we observed that G-MDSCs MHC-II expressing CD80, CD86, or ICOSL correlate positively with phenotypes of CD4 + T cells that produce IL-17 and IFN-γ. For this reason, we suggest that MHC-II + G-MDSC cells may contribute to an inflammatory environment that triggers tissue damage in the lungs of SLE mice.

items.title: An association study suggests that PTPN22 and TNFAIP3, but not STAT4, are risk factors for IgG4-related disease.
items.abstract: To evaluate whether the PTPN22 C1858T (R620W), TNFAIP3 rs2230926T/G (Phe127Cys) and rs6920220G/A, and STAT4 rs7574865G/T variants are risk factors for IgG4-related disease (IgG4-RD). Patients with a diagnosis of IgG4-RD were included. For each patient, two sex-matched healthy controls were included. Genotyping was performed using TaqMan® assays. Statistical analyses were conducted with SNPStats to assess the association between genetic variants and disease susceptibility. Potential gene-gene interactions were evaluated using the multifactor dimensionality reduction approach. We included 60 patients with IgG4-RD and 116 healthy controls. The allelic and genotypic frequencies of the STAT4 rs7574865G/T variant showed no statistically significant differences between cases and controls. In contrast, the PTPN22 rs2476601C/T variant was significantly associated with IgG4-RD under the allelic (C vs. T; OR=10.2, 95% CI 1.18-88.52, p=0.009), codominant (CC vs. CT; OR=10.6, 95% CI 1.21-93.37, p=0.009), and dominant (CC vs. CT+TT; OR=10.6, 95% CI 1.21-93.37, p=0.009) models. Additionally, the TNFAIP3 rs2230926T/G SNV showed the following associations: T vs. G (OR=2.75, 95% CI 0.99-7.60, p=0.04); TT vs TG (OR=2.92, 95% CI 1.03-8.3, p=0.037); and TT vs. TG+GG (OR=2.92, 95% CI 1.03-8.3, p=0.037). Our study identifies the PTPN22 rs2476601C/T and TNFAIP3 rs2230926T/G variants as genetic susceptibility factors for IgG4-RD in the Mexican Mestizo population.

items.title: Tubuloreticular Inclusions in Kidney Tissues of Patients With Lupus Nephritis: An Ultrastructural Biomarker of Type I Interferon-Driven Disease Activity.
items.abstract: Tubuloreticular inclusions (TRIs) in kidney tissues associate with type I interferon (IFN-I) pathway activation, but their clinical and pathological significance in lupus nephritis (LN) remains incompletely defined. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 327 patients with biopsy-confirmed LN at the National Clinical Research Center for Kidney Diseases from January 2023 to December 2025. TRIs were identified in kidney tissues by transmission electron microscopy in both glomerular endothelial cells (GECs) and peritubular capillary (PTC) endothelial cells. For semi-quantitative assessment, 10 capillary loops per glomerulus and 10 peritubular capillaries per case were examined; in cases with more than one glomerulus, loops were randomly selected from each glomerulus and the maximum score across all glomeruli was recorded as the GEC-TRI grade. The final TRI grade for each case was defined as the higher of the GEC-TRI and PTC-TRI grades, classified as grade 0 (no TRIs), grade 1 (TRIs in 1 of 10 capillary profiles) or grade 2 (TRIs in ≥2 of 10 capillary profiles), with patients subsequently grouped as TRI-negative (grade 0) or TRI-positive (grade 1 or 2). Clinical, pathological, immunofluorescence and extrarenal manifestations were compared between groups. In a subset, peripheral blood RNA sequencing was performed to calculate IFN-I scores and assess pathway activation. TRIs were observed in 207 of 327 patients (63.3%). Pathologically, TRI-positive patients exhibited lower chronicity index, higher frequency of segmental loop necrosis, along with reduced rates of vascular lesions, interstitial fibrosis and tubular atrophy (all p < 0.05). On immunofluorescence, increased deposition of IgM and C1q and a higher prevalence of full-house pattern were observed in TRI-positive patients (all p < 0.05); C3 deposition showed a significant stepwise increase across TRI grades (p = 0.03), though the dichotomized comparison was not significant (p = 0.06). Clinically, they had higher SLE Disease Activity Index scores, increased urinary red blood cell counts and elevated proteinuria (all p < 0.05). They also demonstrated lower serum complement levels, increased immunoglobulin levels (e.g., IgA) and higher prevalence of multiple autoantibodies (e.g., anti-dsDNA; all p < 0.05). TRI-positive patients also showed heightened IFN-I signatures and higher prevalence of extrarenal manifestations, including mucocutaneous, musculoskeletal, hematological, pulmonary involvement, serositis and organic brain syndrome (all p < 0.05). TRIs are highly prevalent in kidney tissues of patients with LN. They identify a distinct IFN-I-driven disease subset, offering a practical histopathological marker of heightened activity and potential target for therapeutic stratification. Lupus nephritis (LN) is a serious kidney condition in people with lupus, where the body’s immune system attacks its own healthy tissues. Doctors use blood tests and kidney biopsies to check disease activity, but these tools have limits. This study looked at whether tiny structures called tubuloreticular inclusions (TRIs) – visible only under high-powered electron microscopes – could help identify patients with more active disease. The team examined kidney biopsies from 327 LN patients and compared those with TRIs to those without, looking at symptoms, lab tests, kidney tissue and immune activity. In some patients, they also measured type I interferon activity – an immune pathway overactive in lupus. TRIs were found in 63.3% of patients. Those with TRIs had higher disease activity scores, lower levels of certain immune proteins and more antibodies that attack the body's own cells – all signs of active disease. Their blood also showed higher interferon levels, a sign of immune overactivity. These patients had less kidney scarring, suggesting their disease might be easier to reverse. Finding TRIs in kidney biopsies may help identify LN patients with a disease driven by high interferon activity, and since newer treatments target this immune pathway, these patients might benefit from more personalized care.

items.title: Clinical Features Suggestive of Underlying Eosinophilic Granulomatosis With Polyangiitis Before Dupilumab Therapy in Patients With Chronic Rhinosinusitis With Nasal Polyps.
items.abstract: Dupilumab is effective for eosinophilic chronic rhinosinusitis (ECRS); however, eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) may become clinically apparent after treatment initiation. We retrospectively reviewed three patients with chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps who developed systemic manifestations leading to a diagnosis of EGPA shortly after dupilumab initiation. All three patients had bronchial asthma and peripheral eosinophilia before treatment. EGPA developed within two weeks to two months after dupilumab initiation, with manifestations including fever, arthralgia, peripheral neuropathy, weight loss, and hypertrophic pachymeningitis. Two patients achieved remission with systemic corticosteroids and mepolizumab, whereas one patient with pre-existing myeloperoxidase-antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (MPO-ANCA) positivity had a fatal outcome despite intensive immunosuppressive therapy. Their pretreatment courses suggested that systemic eosinophilic disease may already have been evolving before biologic therapy, particularly in the patient with pre-existing MPO-ANCA positivity. Notably, the timing at which EGPA criteria were fulfilled differed between Japan's Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW) diagnostic criteria and the European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology/American College of Rheumatology (EULAR/ACR) classification criteria in these patients, highlighting that reliance on a single set of criteria may delay recognition of evolving EGPA. These cases emphasize the importance of evaluating unexplained marked eosinophilia, ANCA positivity, and systemic symptoms before initiating dupilumab and of distinguishing transient treatment-associated eosinophilia from emerging systemic vasculitis during follow-up.

items.title: Factors Associated With Systemic Lupus International Collaborating Clinics/American College of Rheumatology (SLICC/ACR) Damage Index-Defined Organ Damage in Patients with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus: A Cross-Sectional Study From Bangladesh.
items.abstract: Introduction Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a chronic autoimmune disease with a wide range of clinical manifestations and an unpredictable course. Although disease activity can fluctuate over time, some organ injury becomes permanent and contributes substantially to the long-term burden of SLE. The Systemic Lupus International Collaborating Clinics/American College of Rheumatology Damage Index (SLICC/ACR DI or SDI) provides a standardized way to capture such irreversible damage. Data describing the burden and clinical correlates of SDI-defined damage in Bangladesh remain limited. This study therefore examined the pattern of established organ damage and the clinical and laboratory factors associated with it among Bangladeshi patients with SLE. Methodology This single-center, cross-sectional observational study included 168 consecutive patients with SLE who fulfilled the 2019 European League Against Rheumatism/American College of Rheumatology classification criteria. Irreversible damage was assessed using the SDI, with a score of ≥1 defining established damage. Demographic, clinical, disease activity, and laboratory characteristics were compared between patients with and without established damage. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors independently associated with damage. A sensitivity analysis excluded patients with a disease duration of <1 year. Because antiphospholipid antibody (aPL) results were available for only 48 participants, aPL status was examined separately in an exploratory nested analysis. Results We identified established organ damage in 51 (30.4%) patients. Among those with damage, 39 (76.5%) had an SDI score of 1. Skin involvement was the most frequently recorded damage domain, affecting 30 (17.9%) patients and 30 (58.8%) of those with established damage. In the primary multivariable model, longer disease duration (adjusted odds ratio (aOR) 1.11 per year, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.02-1.20; P = 0.019), anemia (aOR 2.58, 95% CI 1.22-5.46; P = 0.013), and vasculitis (aOR 4.68, 95% CI 1.70-12.91; P = 0.003) were independently associated with established damage. The Safety of Estrogens in Lupus Erythematosus National Assessment-Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Disease Activity Index (SELENA-SLEDAI) was not independently associated with damage after adjustment (aOR 1.05 per point, 95% CI 0.99-1.11; P = 0.086). After excluding 20 patients with a disease duration of <1 year, anemia and vasculitis remained associated with damage, whereas disease duration and SELENA-SLEDAI did not. In the exploratory analysis of 48 patients with available aPL results, aPL positivity was associated with established damage (aOR 5.95, 95% CI 1.44-24.55; P = 0.014), but the small sample and incomplete testing limit the strength of this finding. Conclusions Established SDI-defined organ damage was present in approximately one-third of patients in this Bangladeshi SLE population, with skin damage being the most common domain. Anemia and vasculitis showed the most consistent associations with established damage, including after exclusion of patients with very early disease. Because the study was cross-sectional, these findings represent associations rather than causal relationships. The exploratory association between aPL positivity and damage should be tested in larger studies with systematic antibody assessment.

items.title: Associations of ECG-derived markers with clinical and biological characteristics in systemic sclerosis: preliminary findings from the SCAR-SSc study.
items.abstract: Cardiac involvement in systemic sclerosis (SSc) is often subclinical in its early stages. Electrocardiographic markers have been associated with arrhythmias and myocardial remodeling and may provide insight into cardiac involvement in SSc. This pilot single-center cross-sectional study explored associations between ECG-derived parameters and clinical and biological features in patients with SSc without overt cardiovascular disease. Thirty-four patients meeting the 2013 American College of Rheumatology/European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology classification criteria were included. N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) and high-sensitivity troponin I were measured, standard 12-lead ECGs were analyzed for interatrial block (IAB), morphology-voltage-P-wave duration (MVP) score and fragmented QRS (fQRS), and 24-hour Holter monitoring was used to quantify arrhythmias. Participants were 85.3% women, with a median (IQR) age of 53.6 (46-61) years and disease duration of 7.95 (1.5-14.8) years; 76.5% had limited cutaneous SSc. Fragmented QRS was present in 7 of 32 patients with evaluable fQRS data (21.9%), and its presence was associated with a higher premature ventricular contraction count on Holter monitoring after adjustment for age and sex (OR = 1.0022; 95% CI, 1.0001-1.0044; P = 0.044). Partial IAB was present in 4 of 8 patients (50%) with diffuse cutaneous SSc. The modified Rodnan skin score (mRSS) differed between patients with and without IAB (9 ± 9 versus 3 ± 4, P = 0.040). Higher MVP scores were associated with mRSS (β = 0.422, P = 0.026), C-reactive protein (β = 0.412, P = 0.028) and NT-proBNP (β = 0.557, P = 0.003). ECG-derived markers were associated with measures of disease severity, ventricular ectopy and NT-proBNP levels. These exploratory findings require confirmation in larger studies.

items.title: Fc N-glycosylation heterogeneity of anti-MDA5 IgG is associated with interstitial lung disease severity via regulating FcγR/C1q signaling in MDA5 + dermatomyositis: a cross‑sectional study.
items.abstract: To characterize Fc N-glycosylation patterns of disease-specific IgG (DSIgG) in anti-MDA5-positive dermatomyositis (MDA5 + DM) and evaluate their associations with interstitial lung disease (ILD) severity. Eighty-four patients with MDA5 + DM and 60 healthy controls were enrolled. Disease-specific anti-MDA5 IgG glycopeptides were analyzed by UPLC-MS/MS. Associations between glycoform features and ILD severity were assessed using correlation analysis, ROC analysis, and logistic regression. Surface plasmon resonance and in vitro functional assays were used to compare glycoform-dependent engagement of FcγRIIa, FcγRIIIa, and C1q, as well as downstream ADCP, ADCC, CDC, and endothelial inflammatory responses. Compared with controls, DSIgG1 from patients with MDA5 + DM showed higher fucosylation and lower sialylation. Severe ILD was associated with increased DSIgG1F and decreased DSIgG1S. In multivariable analysis, lower DSIgG1S remained independently associated with severe ILD (OR = 0.07, p = 0.0065), and DSIgG1S showed strong discriminatory performance for severe ILD (AUC = 0.9133). Functionally, G1S exhibited stronger FcγRIIa-related binding and phagocytic activity, whereas G1F displayed stronger FcγRIIIa and C1q binding, together with increased ADCC and CDC. In endothelial-cell experiments, the two glycoforms induced distinct inflammatory response patterns. Anti-MDA5 DSIgG Fc glycosylation is associated with ILD severity in MDA5 + DM. Distinct glycoforms exhibit differential FcγR/C1q-related effector profiles, supporting a potential role for Fc glycosylation heterogeneity in disease stratification and pathogenesis.

items.title: Nanocatalytic anti-inflammatory therapy for alleviating rheumatoid lesions with endothelial cell-derived hydrosilicene.
items.abstract: Severe inflammatory damage of soft tissues and progressive bone destruction are hallmark features of rheumatoid arthritis (RA), in which over-activated neutrophils and excessive neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) play a pivotal role during the early stages of the disease. Conventional drug therapies, such as methotrexate (MTX), are often insufficient in clinical practice, highlighting the urgent need for more targeted and definitive interventions at disease onset. Recently, accumulating evidences indicate that reactive oxygen species (ROS) act as a key trigger for NETs formation. In this study, we developed a biomimetic nanocatalytic system by coating hydrosilicene (HSI) nanosheets with natural endothelial cell membranes (HSI@ECM). This bio-inspired design mimicked typical endothelial-neutrophil adhesion, enabling targeted delivery of the nanosystem to over-activated neutrophils at the inflammatory sites. The fabricated HSI@ECM subsequently released hydrogen gas in situ and selectively scavenged excessive ROS within the neutrophils, thereby inhibiting NETs formation and preserving mitochondrial function. In vivo experiments in a collagen-induced arthritis (CIA) mouse model demonstrated that HSI@ECM significantly alleviated joint swelling, inflammatory cell infiltration and cartilage-bone damage, outperforming both the uncoated nanosheets and MTX. Overall, this work presents a nanocatalytic anti-inflammatory therapeutic strategy with promising potential for mitigating rheumatoid soft tissue, cartilage and bone damage.

items.title: Clinical and laboratory outcomes during sequential anakinra and canakinumab treatment in familial Mediterranean fever: a retrospective within-patient study.
items.abstract: To describe clinical, laboratory, disease-severity, and safety outcomes after switching from anakinra to canakinumab in FMF patients who required treatment change because of inadequate response and/or intolerance to anakinra. This retrospective within-patient sequential cohort study included 26 adult FMF patients who received anakinra followed by canakinumab between January 2017 and September 2024. Demographic, clinical, genetic, laboratory, treatment-related data, and reasons for switching were obtained from medical records. Annual attack count, C-reactive protein (CRP), erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), 24-h proteinuria, International Severity Score for FMF (ISSF), attack manifestations, and adverse events were evaluated using paired analyses. items.title: Rheumatoid factor positivity in ANCA-negative eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis: cardiac mimicry, mononeuritis multiplex, and long-term outcome in a case-based systematic review.
items.abstract: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) is a rare small- to medium-vessel vasculitis characterized by asthma, eosinophilia, and multisystem involvement. Diagnosis is challenging in ANCA-negative disease, particularly when misleading serology is present. We describe a 42-year-old woman with long-standing asthma and a rheumatoid factor (RF) of 322 IU/mL, who initially presented with myocardial infarction-like cardiac involvement with non-obstructive coronary arteries. Over the subsequent seven months, progressive eosinophilia, chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyposis, and mononeuritis multiplex emerged. ANCA-negative EGPA was diagnosed after connective tissue disease, infection, malignancy, and other causes of hypereosinophilia were excluded. She was treated with prednisolone and azathioprine and subsequently remained off immunosuppressive therapy for more than nine years without reported relapse. On later clinical reassessment, she remained stable apart from mild residual neuropathic symptoms. We also conducted a case-based review following the CABARET standards, searching PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Embase, and Web of Science up to 15 August 2026. We identified 38 published cases of ANCA-negative, RF-positive EGPA, 36 of them without pre-existing rheumatoid arthritis. In these 36, the median age was 53 years and 69% were female. Peripheral neuropathy was reported in 72% and cardiac involvement in 47%; with both occurring in 25%; two patients died of cardiac causes. Among 12 cases with sufficient data to standardize RF relative to the assay upper limit of normal, 75% had RF levels > 3 × ULN. Reporting was often incomplete: both MPO- and PR3-ANCA were documented in only 42% of cases and anti-CCP in 11%. No included published case reported prolonged treatment-free remission, although follow-up and treatment status were incompletely reported in several cases. Based on these gaps, the authors propose a reporting checklist for future EGPA case reports. RF positivity, even at high titer, should not dissuade clinicians from considering EGPA when asthma, eosinophilia, ENT disease, neuropathy, or other compatible manifestations are present.

items.title: The impact of population ageing on rheumatoid arthritis in 204 countries and territories, 1990-2021: global burden and healthcare costs.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a leading cause of disability worldwide, and its global burden is expected to increase further with the ongoing population ageing. Although previous studies have widely evaluated the global burden of RA, few have isolated the independent effect of population ageing from other concurrent factors, such as population growth and changes in epidemiological rates. This study aimed to quantify the impact of population ageing on the global burden and healthcare costs of RA across 204 countries and territories from 1990 to 2021, stratified by geographic region, Socio-demographic Index (SDI) level, and sex. This study represented a secondary analysis of modeled health estimates derived from the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2021 study. A decomposition approach distinguished the effects of population ageing from those of population growth and changes in age-specific epidemiological rates. Healthcare costs attributable to population ageing were estimated through a cost extrapolation method. From 1990 to 2021, population ageing contributed to increases in 145,148 incident cases, 3514328 prevalent cases, and 690,372 disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) due to RA globally. It was the largest contributor to the increase in DALYs among 33.3% of countries and territories. SDI levels showed inverted U-shaped associations with the proportions of incident cases, prevalent cases, and DALYs attributable to population ageing, peaking in middle SDI countries. High SDI countries showed the sole reduction in DALY rate, partially offsetting the increases in DALYs driven by population ageing. However, population ageing contributed more to the increases in incident and prevalent cases than changes in epidemiological rates globally, particularly in middle to high SDI countries. Males had higher proportions attributable to population ageing globally, particularly in middle to high SDI countries, whereas females were more affected in low and low-middle SDI countries. In 2021, population ageing accounted for an estimated US$7.88 billion in RA-related healthcare costs, equivalent to 0.008% of global gross domestic product. In approximately one-third of countries and territories, population ageing has emerged as the largest contributor to the increase in RA-related DALYs. Public health strategies tailored to socio-demographic and sex-specific contexts should prioritize prevention, early diagnosis, and cost-effective management to mitigate the escalating global burden of RA attributable to population ageing.

items.title: Comparative selection of cell-penetrating peptides and development of D-Arg9/iRGD dual-functionalized triptolide nanoliposomes for deepened penetration and rheumatoid arthritis therapy.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) nanodelivery remains limited by insufficient cellular uptake and restricted penetration into deeper tissue regions. In this study, five cell-penetrating peptides (CPPs), including L-TAT, L-MPG, L-Lys 9 , L-Arg 9 , and D-Arg 9 , were comparatively evaluated using a unified liposomal platform. Coumarin 6 (C6) was used as a fluorescent tracer to characterize cellular uptake, subcellular fluorescence distribution, and responses of CPP-functionalized liposomes to endocytic inhibitors, while the corresponding triptolide (TP)-loaded formulations were examined for in vitro anti-inflammatory activity and in vivo anti-arthritic efficacy. During the early incubation period, D-Arg 9 @Lipo C6 exhibited relatively high intracellular C6 fluorescence and a broader subcellular distribution. D-Arg 9 @Lipo TP reduced intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) and multiple pro-inflammatory mediators, together with decreased CD86 expression, increased CD206 expression, and modulation of NF-κB-related protein expression. D-Arg 9 was subsequently combined with the tissue-penetrating peptide iRGD to generate D-Arg 9 -iRGD@Lipo TP . In three-dimensional RAW264.7 spheroids, D-Arg 9 -iRGD@Lipo C6 retained stronger C6 fluorescence in deeper spheroid regions and displayed a broader spatial distribution than either D-Arg 9 @Lipo C6 or iRGD@Lipo C6 . The corresponding TP-loaded formulation reduced TNF-α, IL-6, IL-1β, and PGE 2 levels while increasing IL-10 levels. Following intra-articular administration in rats with adjuvant-induced arthritis (AIA), D-Arg 9 -iRGD@Lipo TP attenuated paw swelling, increased the thermal pain threshold, and alleviated joint inflammation, cartilage damage, and bone destruction. No consistent abnormalities were detected in the measured serum biochemical parameters, and hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) examination of major organs revealed no evident histopathological lesions. C6 was used solely as a tracer of formulation-associated fluorescence distribution; accordingly, intracellular and spheroid C6 fluorescence should not be interpreted as a direct measure of TP exposure. These findings suggest that D-Arg 9 enhances liposomal cellular uptake, whereas the incorporation of iRGD further improves distribution into deeper regions of dense three-dimensional tissue-like structures, supporting a peptide-functionalization strategy for concurrently improving cellular uptake and intratissue distribution in local nanodelivery for RA.

items.title: The IgG4ward! Foundation guidelines on the treatment of IgG4-related disease.
items.abstract: IgG4-related disease is a chronic, immune-mediated, systemic condition that presents as tumour-like masses. Since publication of the last international consensus statement on the treatment of IgG4-related disease in 2015, the related literature has expanded considerably, with two phase 3, randomised, placebo-controlled trials published within the past 2 years. This foundation of evidence for treatment decisions justified new, dedicated treatment guidelines. 62 investigators-comprising 52 physicians, one medical reference librarian, eight patients, and one caregiver from 15 countries across six continents-were assembled to form a treatment guidelines group. The physicians had a broad range of specialties and patient representation spanned the full spectrum of organ involvement. The treatment guidelines group generated 183 candidate questions, which were consolidated into 40 final questions approved by the IgG4ward! Advisory Board. These questions formed the basis of a systematic literature search, led by a medical reference librarian, which informed the development of 28 treatment statements. Supporting evidence for each statement was independently graded using the 2011 Oxford Centre for Evidence-Based Medicine Levels of Evidence framework. The 52 physicians voted electronically on their level of agreement with each statement; consensus required more than 80% to agree or strongly agree with the statement, and was reached for 22 of the 28 statements. The evidence base reflects marked recent progress due to the publication of phase 3 clinical trials, although most statements still rely on low-level evidence. This effort provides cohesive, consensus-based guidelines from a geographically and professionally diverse group of experts in IgG4-related disease, reflecting the evolution in the field since 2015. Despite this progress, important knowledge gaps remain, and are highlighted to guide future research.

items.title: Serum IL-33 Concentrations and the IL-12/IFN-? Axis According to Therapeutic Strategy in Rheumatoid Arthritis.
items.abstract: Interleukin-33 (IL-33) is involved in inflammatory pathways relevant to rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and may interact with the IL-12/interferon-gamma (IFN-γ) axis. However, the relationship between circulating IL-33 concentrations and different therapeutic strategies remains incompletely understood. In this prospective observational study with cross-sectional analysis, 189 consecutive RA patients were stratified according to treatment: methotrexate (MTX), MTX plus TNF inhibitors (MTX+TNFi), tocilizumab (TCZ), and DMARD-naïve patients. Serum IL-33 concentrations were measured by ELISA. Disease activity indices (DAS28-ESR, CDAI, SDAI), inflammatory markers, and serum IL-12 and IFN-γ levels were assessed. IL-33 concentrations differed across therapeutic groups, with the highest levels observed in DMARD-naïve patients and lower levels in those receiving biologic therapy, particularly TCZ. IL-33 was associated with disease activity parameters and showed a modest positive correlation with IL-12. IFN-γ concentrations also differed among treatment groups, with the lowest levels observed in TCZ-treated patients. Serum IL-33 concentrations varied across therapeutic groups in rheumatoid arthritis and were associated with selected indicators of inflammatory activity. Further studies are needed to clarify the role of IL-33 in the immunopathology of rheumatoid arthritis.

items.title: A "Capture-and-Lock" Ozone-Reservoir Hydrogel for Rheumatoid Arthritis Therapy.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease driven by excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) and M1 polarization, leading to synovial inflammation and bone destruction. Current immunosuppressants cannot target these core mechanisms and cause severe side effects. Ozone shows potential for RA treatment via anti-oxidant and anti-inflammatory effects, but its instability, rapid diffusion, and short retention severely limit clinical efficacy. Herein, we develop an injectable ozone-reservoir hydrogel (O3@F@OHC) by covalently incorporating perfluorinated polymer (PFAM) into a Schiff-base crosslinked network of oxidized hyaluronic acid and carboxymethyl chitosan. The hydrogel achieves stable ozone loading and sustained release for over 48 h through a "capture-and-lock" mechanism, with PFAM acting as an efficient "ozone sponge". This hydrogel also exhibits favorable self-healing, biocompatibility, and adaptive biodegradability. In vitro, ozone released from O3@F@OHC hydrogel could activate endogenous antioxidant defense system, thereby enhances cellular antioxidant capacity, eliminates excessive intracellular free radicals, downregulates inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS) expression, and ultimately exerts anti-inflammatory effects. In rats with collagen-induced arthritis, this hydrogel alleviates synovial inflammation and bone destruction. This work provides a promising strategy for ozone-based intra-articular therapy of RA.

items.title: Early recurrence of ANCA-associated vasculitis within one month of kidney transplantation.
items.abstract: Recurrence of antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)-associated vasculitis (AAV) after kidney transplantation is relatively uncommon due to modern immunosuppressive regimens, with early recurrence being particularly rare. We present the case of a 70-year-old woman with end-stage kidney disease of uncertain etiology who developed a biopsy-proven recurrence of pauci-immune crescentic glomerulonephritis within 1 month of receiving a deceased donor kidney transplant. Her initial allograft function was excellent but was followed by a rapid rise in serum creatinine, microscopic hematuria, and proteinuria by post-operative day 20. Serology confirmed a high p-ANCA titer. She was treated with pulse steroids and rituximab, with subsequent stabilization of her kidney function. This case highlights that AAV can recur very early in the post-transplant period and underscores the critical need to maintain a high index of suspicion for recurrent or de novo pauci-immune glomerulonephritis in transplant recipients with early allograft dysfunction, especially when the cause of their native kidney disease is unclear.

items.title: Artemisinin-Loaded Core-Shell Microspheres Modulate Histone Lactylation to Remodel the Microenvironment for Cartilage Protection in Rheumatoid Arthritis.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) involves persistent inflammation and metabolic dysregulation that jointly drive cartilage damage. Although lactate accumulates in arthritic joints, the role of lactate-induced histone lactylation in cartilage progenitor cell (CPC) dysfunction remains unclear. Here, we developed an injectable, tissue-adhesive core-shell microsphere (ART@PLGA@GH-A) for sustained intra-articular delivery of artemisinin (ART). CUT&Tag sequencing identified a pathological lactate-H4K16la-Ccnb2 axis in RA-derived CPCs, in which lactate accumulation enhanced H4K16la enrichment at the Ccnb2 promoter, promoting mitochondrial dysfunction, cellular senescence, and extracellular matrix degradation. ART@PLGA@GH-A suppressed H4K16la deposition at the Ccnb2 locus and more effectively inhibited CPC senescence and glycolytic lactate production than ART-loaded hydrogel microspheres (ART@GH). Mechanistically, ART@PLGA@GH-A promoted macrophage polarization from pro-inflammatory M1 toward anti-inflammatory M2, reduced intracellular and mitochondrial reactive oxygen species, restored mitochondrial membrane potential and dynamics, enhanced chondrogenic markers (COL II, Aggrecan, and SOX9), and reduced matrix-degrading enzymes (MMP13 and ADAMTS5). In collagen-induced arthritis rats, a single intra-articular injection of ART@PLGA@GH-A reduced subchondral bone erosion and proteoglycan loss and improved hindlimb gait function, outperforming free ART and non-adhesive microspheres. Therefore, ART@PLGA@GH-A targets the lactate-dependent H4K16la-Ccnb2 axis and restores joint homeostasis, thereby achieving synergistic anti-inflammatory, anti-senescent, and chondroprotective effects and providing a clinically translatable local therapeutic strategy for RA.

items.title: CD163+ macrophage infiltration reflects disease activity and early treatment response in lupus nephritis.
items.abstract: Lupus nephritis (LN) is a severe manifestation of systemic lupus erythematosus, potentially leading to progressive kidney damage and end-stage kidney disease. Emerging evidence suggests that macrophages play a key role in LN pathogenesis. The aim of this study was to investigate associations between renal macrophage infiltration and clinical, histopathological, and long-term renal outcomes in LN. This retrospective cohort study included 58 biopsy-proven LN patients (2002-2018), with a mean follow-up of 77 months. Immunohistochemistry for CD68, CD163, CD206, and C5aR1 macrophage markers was performed on baseline kidney biopsies. Correlations with histological features and clinical parameters such as kidney function (eGFR), proteinuria and long-term renal outcomes were analysed using correlation matrices and linear mixed models. CD163+ macrophage infiltration in glomerular and tubulointerstitial compartments was significantly associated with clinical and histological activity, including lower baseline eGFR, lower complement levels, more leukocyturia/erythrocyturia and higher activity index scores. Patients with high CD163+ infiltration demonstrated significantly greater improvement of eGFR and proteinuria during the first 6 months of treatment post-diagnosis. Conversely, low CD163+ infiltration was associated with increased likelihood of requiring a repeat biopsy. These associations were not observed when stratifying by LN class. CD68+ macrophages showed a similar trend. CD206+ and C5aR1+ macrophages were not associated with markers of disease activity, although high glomerular C5aR1+ infiltration was linked to repeat biopsy. None of the macrophage markers were associated with long-term outcomes such as renal flares, dialysis, or transplantation. CD163+ macrophage infiltration at baseline is associated with active disease and early treatment response in LN, independent of received treatment. While LN class guides treatment choice, CD163+ macrophage infiltration may offer additional prognostic value regarding early therapeutic response. These findings support further investigation of CD163+ macrophages as a biomarker not only providing prognostic information but also helping guide treatment choices beyond the current LN classification system.

items.title: WTAP regulates PTEN through m6A methylation to modulate the inflammatory response in CD4+ T cells from patients with ankylosing spondylitis.
items.abstract: This study aimed to investigate how Wilms' tumour 1-related protein (WTAP)-mediated m6A methylation regulates PTEN and thereby influences the inflammatory response in ankylosing spondylitis (AS) through a combination of a case-control study and cellular experiments. Peripheral venous blood (10 mL) was drawn from each participant, and CD4+ T lymphocytes were isolated using a human positive selection kit. mRNA expression levels of WTAP and PTEN were measured by quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR). Plasma was separated by centrifugation and subjected to enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) to quantify inflammatory cytokine concentrations. A WTAP-knockdown model was established in human Jurkat T cells using small interfering RNA (siRNA), followed by analysis of downstream gene transcription and protein expression via qRT-PCR and Western blotting, respectively. After WTAP knockdown, the m6A modification level of PTEN mRNA in Jurkat cells was determined by MeRIP-qPCR. Results showed that WTAP and PTEN expression levels in CD4+ T lymphocytes were significantly downregulated in AS patients compared to healthy controls, and both were inversely correlated with TNF-α levels. Moreover, WTAP knockdown in Jurkat T cells led to a marked decrease in both PTEN expression and its m6A modification, which coincided with a significant increase in TNF-α expression. In conclusion, WTAP downregulation promotes AS inflammation by decreasing PTEN expression through an m6A-dependent mechanism.

items.title: Systematic evaluation of animal models for systemic sclerosis-associated interstitial lung disease: focus on pulmonary and extrapulmonary pathophysiology.
items.abstract: Systemic sclerosis-associated interstitial lung disease (SSc-ILD) is a major driver of mortality in systemic sclerosis and a prototypical fibroinflammatory disorder in which pulmonary fibrosis unfolds alongside systemic immune, vascular and extrapulmonary abnormalities. Across bleomycinbased, chemical, genetic and immunemediated platforms, striking differences emerge in disease spectrum, reproducibility and biological relevance, and few models recapitulate the integrated fibroinflammatory, immune and vascular complexity of human SSc-ILD.This unresolved gap continues to constrain mechanistic insight and therapeutic development. Advancing the field will require next-generation models that more closely reflect the complexity, chronicity and heterogeneity of human SSc-ILD.

items.title: Rheumatoid Arthritis and Sleep Disturbances: A Narrative Review of Bidirectional Mechanisms.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a systemic autoimmune disease in which sleep disturbances are common and closely linked to pain, fatigue, mood symptoms, physical dysfunction, and disease activity. This narrative review synthesizes clinical and mechanistic evidence for a bidirectional relationship between RA and impaired sleep while distinguishing diagnosed sleep disorders from transdiagnostic sleep symptoms. RA-related inflammation, pain, stiffness, and psychological comorbidity may impair sleep through peripheral-to-central inflammatory signaling, altered monoamine metabolism, circadian disruption, hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis dysfunction, autonomic hyperarousal, and central sensitization. Conversely, insufficient or fragmented sleep may disrupt immune and circadian homeostasis, amplify pro-inflammatory signaling and pain sensitivity, and thereby worsen RA symptoms and possibly disease activity. However, much of the available evidence is cross-sectional, based on patient-reported sleep, or derived from small treatment studies, so direct causality and the independent contribution of individual pathways remain uncertain. Evidence from cytokine-blocking and sleep-directed interventions suggests potential benefit, but improvements may be mediated through changes in pain, fatigue, mood, and inflammatory activity. Age, sex, adiposity, medications, depression, anxiety, and sleep-disorder phenotype further modify these associations. Clinically, RA care should distinguish insomnia, obstructive sleep apnea, restless legs syndrome, circadian problems, and non-diagnostic sleep symptoms, then combine optimized RA and pain management with disorder-specific sleep treatment. Longitudinal multimodal cohorts and adequately powered trials using both patient-reported and objective sleep outcomes are priorities.

items.title: The Association Between Oxidative Balance Score and All-Cause Mortality in Patients With Rheumatoid Arthritis.
items.abstract: This study aimed to explore the associations of the oxidative balance score (OBS) and all-cause and cardiovascular disease (CVD) mortality in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA), and to analyze the mediating role of the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR). Data were obtained from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey. Cox proportional hazards models were used to assess the associations of total OBS, dietary OBS, and lifestyle OBS with all-cause and CVD mortality. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis was performed to explore dose-response relationships, while subgroup analysis was conducted to verify the robustness of the results. Mediation analysis examined NLR-mediated association between OBS and all-cause mortality. 887 RA patients were analyzed, with 79 deaths during follow-up. In the fully adjusted model, each 1-unit increase in total OBS, dietary OBS, and lifestyle OBS was associated with a 6%, 7%, and 25% lower risk of all-cause mortality, respectively. Total OBS was negatively associated with CVD mortality when analyzed as a continuous variable, but not when categorized into tertiles. RCS analysis confirmed linear dose-response relationships between total OBS, dietary OBS, lifestyle OBS, and all-cause mortality. NLR mediated a small proportion of the associations of total OBS (5.47%) and dietary OBS (4.89%) with all-cause mortality. Subgroup analysis showed that the negative association between total OBS and all-cause mortality across several subgroups. Higher total OBS, dietary OBS, and lifestyle OBS were significantly associated with reduced all-cause mortality in RA patients, with a linear dose-response relationship.

items.title: Elevated lactate dehydrogenase and co-infection: predictors of rapidly progressive interstitial lung disease and fatal outcomes in anti-MDA5-positive dermatomyositis.
items.abstract: To identify predictors of adverse outcomes in hospitalised patients with anti-melanoma differentiation-associated gene 5 antibody-positive dermatomyositis (anti-MDA5+ DM). We retrospectively analysed data from 113 anti-MDA5+ DM patients during their first hospitalisation, including clinical features, season of onset, high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) and laboratory results. Patients presenting primarily with respiratory symptoms had a significantly poorer prognosis than those with skin/muscle symptoms (p<0.05). Onset in winter/spring was associated with higher co-infection rates (p<0.05), and co-infected patients had higher rates of rapidly progressive interstitial lung disease (RP-ILD) or death (p<0.05). Serum lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) levels were significantly higher in patients with RP-ILD or death (p<0.05). Respiratory symptoms, co-infection, and elevated LDH (≥ 324.5 IU/L) are independent risk factors for RP-ILD or death in anti-MDA5+ DM. For newly hospitalised patients, detailed symptom assessment, prompt infection screening (especially with winter/spring onset) and close LDH monitoring are crucial for prognosis evaluation and guiding clinical management.

items.title: Glycolipid metabolic changes during remission induction in ANCA-associated vasculitis: a retrospective study of the lipid paradox.
items.abstract: To investigate dynamic changes in glycolipid metabolism in patients with antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody-associated vasculitis (AAV) during remission induction and to explore their associations with inflammatory markers, treatment and ANCA antigen specificity. In this retrospective cohort study of 973 patients with AAV, baseline glycolipid profiles and the prevalence of dyslipidaemia were assessed. Paired baseline and post-remission induction glycolipid parameters were compared in the longitudinal cohort. Multivariable models were used to evaluate factors associated with baseline dyslipidaemia and exploratory associations with metabolic changes. Additional analyses compared patients with and without longitudinal data and assessed the relationship between changes in inflammatory markers and metabolic parameters. Dyslipidaemia was highly prevalent at baseline. Inflammatory markers, including erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and C-reactive protein (CRP), were associated with dyslipidaemia. During remission induction, triglyceride, total cholesterol and LDL-C levels increased, whereas fasting glucose and the TC/HDL-C ratio decreased, consistent with a lipid-paradox pattern. Additional analyses suggested potential selection bias in the longitudinal cohort. Patients with AAV show a high burden of baseline dyslipidaemia and dynamic glycolipid metabolic changes during remission induction. The observed increase in lipid concentrations together with decreases in fasting glucose and the TC/HDL-C ratio suggests a lipid-paradox pattern and a close relationship between inflammation and metabolic status. Further prospective studies with standardised treatment exposure and cardiovascular outcome assessment are needed to clarify the clinical significance of these metabolic trajectories.

items.title: Nailfold capillaroscopy by dermatoscope in systemic sclerosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Nailfold capillaroscopy is pivotal for assessing microvascular abnormalities in systemic sclerosis (SSc), with nailfold videocapillaroscopy (NVC) as the gold standard. However, NVC availability and practicality are limited in routine clinical settings, prompting interest in dermatoscope-based nailfold capillaroscopy (DNC) as an accessible alternative. This review evaluates the diagnostic value of DNC for identifying the scleroderma pattern compared to standard highmagnification techniques. .Systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus and Web of Science per PRISMA-DTA guidelines. Eligible studies assessed sensitivity and specificity of DNC versus NVC or stereomicroscopy in adults. Univariate and bivariate random-effects meta-analysis pooled sensitivity, specificity, diagnostic odds ratio, and area under the Summary Receiver Operating Characteristic (SROC) curve (AUC). Three studies, including 340 participants, met inclusion criteria. Pooled analysis demonstrated sensitivity of 56% (95% CI: 39-80%) and specificity of 95% (95% CI: 91-100%) for DNC in detecting scleroderma capillary patterns. Pooled diagnostic odds ratio was 31.83 (95% CI: 16.85-60.15), with an AUC of 0.895 indicating high diagnostic performance. Limited data demonstrate DNC offers high specificity but moderate sensitivity for identifying scleroderma patterns in SSc, making it a valuable initial screening tool for resource-limited settings in patients with Raynaud's phenomenon. While DNC cannot replace NVC for detailed microvascular assessment, its ease of use, portability, and diagnostic performance support implementation for mainly triage of capillary abnormalities in SSc and connective tissue diseases in routine clinical practice.

items.title: The clinical potential of serum autotaxin levels at diagnosis as a biomarker for current activity and subsequent complications in patients with microscopic polyangiitis and granulomatosis with polyangiitis.
items.abstract: Autotaxin (ATX), a secretory enzyme that primarily converts lysophosphatidylcholine to lysophosphatidic acid, has been proposed as a novel biomarker for inflammatory diseases. In this context, in this study, we investigated the clinical potential of serum ATX levels at diagnosis as a biomarker for current activity and subsequent complications in patients with microscopic polyangiitis (MPA) or granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA). The present study included 72 patients with MPA or GPA. Clinical data at diagnosis and during follow-up were retrospectively reviewed, and serum ATX levels were measured using serum samples collected and stored at diagnosis. Disease activity was assessed using the Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score (BVAS). All-cause mortality (ACM) and end-stage kidney disease were investigated as systemic complications of MPA and GPA. At diagnosis, serum ATX levels were significantly correlated with BVAS, C-reactive protein, and serum albumin levels. Serum ATX levels at diagnosis were significantly higher in deceased patients than in surviving patients. Using a cut-off value of ≥713.9 ng/mL for serum ATAX to predict subsequent ACM, patients with serum ATX ≥713.9 ng/mL exhibited a significantly lower cumulative patients' survival rate than those with serum ATX <713.9 ng/mL. In multivariable Cox proportional hazards analysis, serum ATX ≥713.9 ng/mL was significantly and independently associated with subsequent ACM. In the present study, we demonstrated the clinical potential of serum ATX levels at diagnosis as a useful indicator for assessing current activity and as a predictor of subsequent ACM in patients with MPA or GPA.

items.title: Serum cytokine profiling identifies distinct immune phenotypes in eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis: interleukin-25- and interleukin-5-driven eosinophilic subtypes.
items.abstract: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) is a rare systemic vasculitis characterised by eosinophilia and small vessel inflammation; however, its immunopathology remains incompletely understood. We aimed to elucidate immune dysregulation in EGPA by profiling serum cytokines in treatment-naïve patients in comparison with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), and by longitudinally assessing cytokine dynamics before and after initial therapy as well as during mepolizumab treatment. We quantitatively profiled 31 serum cytokines in 27 patients with EGPA, including treatment-naïve and mepolizumab-treated individuals, and compared the results with those of 26 patients with active SLE. Longitudinal cytokine changes were assessed before and after initial therapy and during mepolizumab treatment. Eosinophil functional assays and quantification of alarmins were also performed. Patients with EGPA exhibited higher levels of Th2 cytokines, particularly IL-5, than those with SLE, whereas Th1 and Th17 cytokine levels were comparable. IL-1 receptor antagonist (IL-1Ra) levels were markedly elevated in EGPA, but not in peripheral eosinophils in vitro. Both IL-1Ra and IL-8 levels decreased after the initial treatment, suggesting their potential as biomarkers of disease activity. Subgroup analysis suggested heterogeneous eosinophilic patterns: one associated with IL-25, and the other with IL-5 in the absence of IL-25. EGPA exhibits heterogeneous and exploratory immunopathological patterns associated with IL-25 detectability or IL-5-associated eosinophilia. These findings provide novel insights into the pathogenesis of EGPA and highlight the potential of cytokine-based stratification for prospective personalised therapeutic approaches.

items.title: Updates in Neuropsychiatric Systemic Lupus Erythematosus: Advances in Pathogenesis, Diagnosis, and Therapies.
items.abstract: Neuropsychiatric systemic lupus erythematosus (NPSLE) encompasses a diverse range of neurological and psychiatric manifestations occurring in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE); however, these events are ultimately attributed to NPSLE only after rigorous exclusion of alternative etiologies and secondary causes. These manifestations result directly from lupus-related inflammation, vascular damage, or autoantibody effects on the central and peripheral nervous systems. The purpose of this review is to provide an updated overview of NPSLE, the multidisciplinary approach in diagnosing NPSLE, the different proposed mechanisms of pathophysiology, as well as the available treatment options. It also sheds light on the introduced advancements in personalized targeted therapy for NPSLE. A comprehensive review of the relevant literature on the state of NPSLE diagnosis, pathogenesis, and treatment was conducted. Different search databases (PubMed, Google Scholar, ScienceDirect) were searched for studies published, prioritizing the most recent ones. Search terms included "neuropsychiatric manifestations of SLE", "diagnostic biomarkers", "targeted therapy", and "autoantibodies and neurotoxicity". Only English-language articles were included. As a narrative review, the selection was not systematic and may be subject to selection bias. The review presented the most evident recent diagnostic approaches of NPSLE, including those currently in clinical use and those still under investigation. Moreover, the complex pathogenesis of autoantibodies, inflammatory cells, and cytokines, along with other environmental and genetic factors, was discussed. The emerging and promising strategies for NPSLE management targeting proposed or emerging pathogenic pathways offer new opportunities to treat one of the most severe complications of SLE. The growing understanding of the pathogenesis of NPSLE paves the way for targeted therapy and symptom management. Despite promising advances, actual clinical trials are needed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of the proposed treatment strategies. Future research should focus on validating the personalized targeted interventions and ultimately improving prognosis and outcomes for patients suffering from this severe complication of NPSLE.

items.title: Occult lung adenocarcinoma diagnosed by EBUS-TBNA after pneumothorax resolution in an RA-ILD patient with respiratory failure.
items.abstract: RA-ILD is a serious complication of RA. Patients are prone to spontaneous pneumothorax and have a higher risk of lung cancer.Given poor lung function and high risk of pneumothorax recurrence, conventional biopsy is challenging, making diagnosis difficult. A 67-year-old male with a history of smoking and well-controlled rheumatoid arthritis presented with chest tightness and pleuritic chest pain. On admission, he was found to have respiratory failure (PaO₂ 58.9mmHg). Chest CT revealed left-sided pneumothorax with interstitial lung disease.Following closed thoracic drainage, the pneumothorax resolved, which was confirmed by follow-up chest X-ray.But the persistence of the patient's chest pain despite resolution of the pneumothorax prompted further investigation.CT pulmonary angiography identified a suspicious mass in the left lower lobe with adjacent rib destruction and mediastinal lymphadenopathy. Given the high risk of recurrent pneumothorax from percutaneous biopsy in a patient with recent pneumothorax and pre-existing respiratory failure, a multidisciplinary team recommended Endobronchial ultrasound-guided transbronchial needle aspiration(EBUS-TBNA) as a safer alternative. EBUS of enlarged mediastinal lymph nodes (stations 7 and 11L) confirmed poorly differentiated lung adenocarcinoma.The patient subsequently received first-line chemotherapy with pemetrexed, cisplatin, and bevacizumab, after which his condition gradually stabilized. Both pneumothorax and interstitial lung disease can mask an occult malignancy, underscoring the need for clinical vigilance. EBUS-TBNA is a safe and effective diagnostic option in such high-risk cases.

items.title: Adaptation and validation of the brief-satisfaction with appearance scale into Hungarian for patients with systemic sclerosis.
items.abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is a chronic autoimmune disease characterized by fibrosis and visible skin changes that often result in body image dissatisfaction and impaired quality of life. Despite this, appearance-related concerns remain under-investigated in SSc. The Brief Satisfaction with Appearance Scale (Brief-SWAP) is a concise, validated instrument designed to assess body image dissatisfaction and social discomfort in individuals with visible disfigurement due to SSc. To adapt and validate the Brief-SWAP scale into Hungarian using internationally accepted methodology. Sixty patients with systemic sclerosis (53 women, 7 men; mean age 57.7 ± 13.5 years; 51.7% diffuse cutaneous SSc) and 31 age- and sex-matched healthy controls (mean age 57.9 ± 14.9 years) participated in the study. The adaptation process followed the OMERACT filter methodology, including forward-backward translation and cultural adaptation. Psychometric evaluation included structural validity (via principal component analysis) reliability (internal consistency and test-retest reliability), construct validity (convergent and discriminant validity) and content validity. Structural validity confirmed a two subdomains model consistent with the original structure: dissatisfaction with appearance and social discomfort. Reliability was high: internal consistency was acceptable (Cronbach's alpha= 0.716; p < 0.001) and test-retest reliability was strong (ICC= 0.828). Regarding construct validity, discriminant validity was demonstrated by significantly higher Brief-SWAP scores in SSc patients versus controls (median 13.0 [IQR 6.0; 18.0] vs. 3.0 [1.0; 9.0]; p < 0.001) with no significant difference between limited and diffuse cutaneous SSc subgroups. Convergent validity showed moderate correlations with depression scales and SF-36 components. Content validity was confirmed, with no floor or ceiling effects observed. The Hungarian version of the Brief-SWAP is a valid and reliable instrument for assessing body image dissatisfaction and its psychosocial impact in patients with SSc. Its brevity and ease of use make it suitable for clinical and research applications focused on health-related quality of life.

items.title: Autoimmune retinal microangiopathy.
items.abstract: To describe a patient with proliferative vascular retinopathy as an ocular complication of an autoimmune connective tissue disease. Case report. A 27-year-old female patient was referred for a regular eye examination, 5 months after the onset of dermatomyositis. On examination, visual acuity was 20/20 in both eyes. The anterior segment was normal. Funduscopy showed microhemorrhages and numerous retinal neovessels in both eyes. The established diagnosis was proliferative vascular retinopathy in dermatomyositis. The patient received treatment with multiple intravitreal anti-VEGF injections. Despite a good response to dermatomyositis treatment with methylprednisolone 4 mg per day and methotrexate 15 mg per week, the retinal neovascularisation reactivated within 3-4 months after anti-VEGF injections. Laser retinal photocoagulation has been performed, and the patient's follow-up continues. Proliferative vascular retinopathy represents an exceedingly rare ocular manifestation of dermatomyositis. The marked bilateral retinal capillary nonperfusion and recurrent neovascularization observed in this patient are consistent with a severe ischemic microangiopathic process, potentially related to immune-mediated endothelial injury. Only isolated cases of proliferative retinopathy associated with overlap connective tissue disease have been reported, underscoring the unusual nature of this case. Proliferative vascular retinopathy may occur secondary to dermatomyositis. All clinicians must recognize this rare association to detect and treat it early.
